articles.title: [OPINION] Next decade of Philippine climate action set in new but incomplete NDC
articles.summary: It is true that we need to secure finance, technologies, and means for capacity-building from developed countries. Yet the impacts of the climate crisis would not stop affecting our economy and…

blocks.text: If our nation got P1,000 every time someone in government mentioned that the Philippines is one of the most climate-vulnerable countries, maybe this country would not be in so much debt.

But the risk we face due to the climate crisis is real and of serious concern. If the past few weeks of flooding or extreme heat — depending on where you live — have not made that apparent, then look at what has happened to our country in the past year or two alone. Or look at Nepal or Indonesia or Antarctica — or almost anywhere else in this world.
This should make us wonder: what is the vision for our response to the climate crisis, especially as we also continue to pursue sustainable development?

On September 8, we got our answer to that question with the publication of the Philippines’ updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), our pledge for climate action as part of the Paris Agreement.

Compared to a “business-as-usual” scenario, the new NDC sets our target for reducing climate pollution by 75% between 2025 and 2035. Of this figure, 7% is unconditional — meaning no foreign assistance is needed to implement climate solutions — from energy efficiency and conservation and some nature-based solutions (NbS) like reforestation.

It is true that we need to secure finance, technologies, and means for capacity-building from developed countries. This is not just because we do need these resources, given the enormity of the problem; it is because those countries are the ones who polluted the world the most on their way to achieving high-income economy status, causing the climate crisis. Polluters must pay.

Yet the impacts of the climate crisis would not stop affecting our economy and society if we just wait for developed countries to fulfill their obligations. We still need to pursue national sustainable development — which necessitates a higher unconditional target.

Is the proposed 2027 national budget actually prioritizing these unconditional climate solutions? If the Marcos Jr. administration truly prioritizes the climate agenda — which the President claimed at the start of his term — then this must be reflected in every national budget until 2035.

Look at our NbS, for example. Using all government-led actions under the third thematic area of our National Climate Change Action Plan as the basis for the scale of its funding, the 2026 funding for NbS is 28 times lower than for climate-tagged new roads, bridges, and other gray infrastructure. It is also five times lower than the ASEAN benchmark for the NbS-to-public expenditures ratio.

A big part of the higher target is due to the full integration of the forestry and other land use sector in the updated NDC, unlike the first version. How much more signs does the government need to invest public funds in ecosystem protection, conservation, and restoration?
You might ask yourself — why does the Philippines need to decrease its climate pollution?
Yes, we do not emit as much pollution as the rich countries. But to paraphrase what a lawmaker said once, the cost of inaction is greater than the cost of action now.

The Philippines has been playing catch-up to the rest of its ASEAN neighbors and the rest of the world on many aspects of development — from public transport to renewable energy. Every climate extreme that hits our country — and there is still a Super El Niño headed our way — forces us to spend more on response and rehabilitation instead of investing in these areas that lead to climate-resilient development that also creates green jobs and ensures food, water, energy, and human security.
This is why implementing the NDC matters. This is why we need to decarbonize as a country.
Yet there are many challenges to which the government has not properly responded, despite calls from civil society groups in recent years.

Among these is the lack of a strong commitment to transitioning away from fossil fuels (TAFF). The national government has refused to join a global coalition of the willing to initiate an approach that everyone will have to do anyway. It has even eased restrictions on the coal moratorium under the guise of advancing projects it considers nationally significant.

The impacts of the war in the Middle East — higher oil prices, inflation in other goods and services, disruptions in work and schooling, among others — should have already taught us the lesson of making the TAFF choice. Instead, the country remains on the path to an energy sector dominated by fossil fuels — which has given us high electricity bills and alerts of different colors on our energy supply.
Sooner or later, the Philippine government will make the TAFF choice. It should have been sooner.

There are still many questions left unanswered in this process of updating our climate pledge. How much of the first NDC submitted in 2021 has been fully implemented? How much would it cost to implement it?

Failing to provide these critical pieces of information is, at the minimum, arguably considered neglect of the national government’s responsibilities in addressing the climate crisis. This is established under the 2025 International Court of Justice Advisory Opinion on climate change, which is politically reaffirmed through a United Nations General Assembly resolution passed this year — one that the Philippines itself voted for.

These global decisions reinforce the 1.5°C warming limit as the benchmark with which we assess whether our government is doing enough to address the climate crisis. Yes, that threshold will be exceeded in at least the next few years, largely because developed countries failed to do what is right.

Yet this should make our country more determined to enact a just transition toward a low-emissions, climate-resilient nation, where no one is left behind. That can start with properly implementing our NDC.
After all, no matter how ambitious a promise is, climate action speaks louder than words. – Rappler.com
John Leo Algo is the national coordinator of Aksyon Klima Pilipinas.

articles.title: NBI: Alan Peter Cayetano not 2019 SEA Games committee chair on paper
articles.summary: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Wednesday said it was having difficulty linking alleged anomalies in the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games to Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano…

blocks.text: Published September 9, 2026 2:47pm

The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Wednesday said it was having difficulty linking alleged anomalies in the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games to Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano due to the lack of a paper trail, noting that he was technically not the chair of the organizing committee.

Cayetano has been closely associated with the 2019 SEA Games controversy after former President Rodrigo Duterte designated him as chair of the Philippine Southeast Asian Games Organizing Committee (PHISGOC).

“There was an instruction to establish and incorporate PHISGOC and register it with the SEC. When it was registered, the Board of Trustees were listed, and he was not among them," NBI Director Melvin Matibag said in an interview with DZBB.
"So he could not be the chairman because he was not a member of the corporation, but he acted as chairman," he added.

Matibag said this was why, despite the NBI's discovery of new evidence that could lead to cases against PHISGOC officials, investigators have struggled to trace the alleged anomalies to Cayetano because his name does not appear on relevant documents.

Despite this, Matibag said Cayetano's actions could constitute usurpation of function because he acted as PHISGOC chair. The NBI chief also cited witness testimonies indicating that Cayetano at times directed where funds should be allocated.

Aside from receiving funds from the Philippine Olympic Committee, Philippine Sports Commission and Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation for the SEA Games, PHISGOC also oversaw ticket sales and revenues, according to Matibag.
He also said that although PHISGOC was established for the 2019 SEA Games, the organization has continued to function to this day.
“Until now, they sponsor international events using PHISGOC, and they are benefiting from government-granted benefits, including exemptions,” Matibag said.
GMA News has reached out to Cayetano’s office for comment and will update this story once it responds.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: BRICS leaders gather in India, but does the group have a clear purpose?
articles.summary: The 18th BRICS summit takes place in India this weekend. Unlike last year, the leaders of China and Russia are coming. But does the expanded group have a clear common mission and purpose?

image.caption: This year's BRICS host India has to balance welcoming new members like Iran without appearing to snub the USImage: Qamar Sibtain/IANS

blocks.text: In preparation for hosting the 18th BRICS summit in Delhi this weekend, India came up with a slogan which tried to keep the group's brand intact without alienating its many new members.

"Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability" matches the acronym for the body's five original members — Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa — whilst also denoting goals which the new members — Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates — can get behind.

"It's an elegant way to reinterpret BRICS so that the acronym represents a joint mission rather than country names," Mihaela Papa, director of the BRICS Lab at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, told DW.
For Sushant Singh, lecturer in South Asian Studies at Yale University, the vague slogan reflects India's desire as hosts to keep BRICS as low-key and neutral as possible.
"India doesn't want to offend Russia or China, but the fact is that Indians are looking more towards the United States these days. The desire to build up BRICS is not there."
India takes host role
Yet host India's status as a rising global geopolitical power has added clout to this year's gathering when compared with last year's summit in Brazil.

At the Rio de Janeiro gathering, six of the bloc's 11 heads of state skipped the event, including major players like Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Putin is expected to attend, while Xi Jinping is widely expected but not yet formally confirmed by Beijing.
"The participation of China's top leadership is crucial," says Papa.
She also thinks it would be a significant sign of the BRICS' strength as a "stabilizing force" if the leaders of regional rivals Iran and the UAE were shown to be able to work together.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian will attend but UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan is expected to send representatives. Saudi Arabia, another Iranian foe, is also expected to. The country's BRICS status remains somewhat ambiguous, although current official BRICS materials generally list it as a member.

blocks.caption: Several heads of state skipped the 2025 gatheringImage: Fabio Teixeira/Anadolu/picture alliance

blocks.text: For India, the summit is as significant for the bilateral meetings it brings as much as for the BRICS gathering itself. Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi are due to meet on Friday while the summit will also present an opportunity for Xi and Modi to speak face-to-face amid continued strain in the China-India relationship.
However, that does not mean much of substance will emerge from the weekend.
"In terms of concrete outcomes and what is achievable, I think it's going to be very, very limited," says Singh.

Modi has spoken of BRICS as an important forum for the 'Global South' to present a common front on various issues. He has also spoken about "a people-centric approach" and the spirit of "humanity first".
However, Singh says BRICS is simply not a priority for India and that in general, Delhi has not appreciated what many have interpreted as the "anti-western" turn the group has taken in recent times.
"With India as chair, India won't be comfortable with any kind of anti-western line," he says, pointing to the focus it places on defense ties with the US and trade ties with the west as a whole.

blocks.caption: The leaders of Russia, China and India will all be present this yearImage: REUTERS/ANI

blocks.text: "India's idea of BRICS is more to look at improving trade ties, etc. In other words, can we do things which are beneficial to us without in any way being confrontational or critical of the West?"
Yet ironically, India's non-aligned status means it may actually be able to keep the bloc aligned.

"India adds clout because it has significant geopolitical weight and relationships across competing camps, making it an important bridge-builder," says Papa. "Its approach is likely to keep BRICS focused on practical cooperation and global governance reform rather than overt bloc politics."
What is BRICS for anyway?
BRICS is soon approaching its 18th birthday, so in a sense it should be coming of age. Yet the bloc has struggled for coherence in recent years amid doubt over its purpose.
The scale of what it could represent is not in doubt. It boasts nearly half the world's population among its members and around 40% of its GDP.

Last year, its joint declaration called for reforms of global governance, specifying representation on multilateral bodies such as the IMF and the World Bank. It also condemned tariffs and decried what it called the "polarization" of the international order.
"Ideologically, BRICS remains where it was during the last summit in Brazil, focused on practical, functional cooperation while seeking to avoid geopolitical tensions," says Papa.

blocks.caption: BRICS foreign ministers have already met ahead of the summitImage: ANI

blocks.text: She says that the expansion of the group from five to 11 members — if we include Saudi Arabia — has made it harder to reach consensus on various issues.

There are also now more autocracies among its members than democracies, while many members have tense bilateral relations. "These internal contradictions will always be hard to reconcile," says Singh.
What might happen this year

Nonetheless, Papa says she expects progress this year in three areas: trade, monetary cooperation, and agriculture. Discussions are likely to focus on improving trade between the members, alternative financial architecture for exchanging currencies and on issues around food security.

While talk of reforming global governance will still be central, she thinks BRICS' best hope to focus on the institutions which it agrees most on. For example, India is reluctant to press for UN reform but is keen for a co-ordinated approach from BRICS to trade and the WTO.
"India's WTO ambitions are shared by more members," she says, which makes movement in that area "more likely."
Yet many still share Singh's view that the group will "continue to underwhelm."
He says issues ranging from China's growing global dominance to the Trump administration's stance on tariffs have made the bloc's limited goals even harder to achieve.
"With the kind of world that we are in and the lack of coherence and internal contradictions that BRICS has, it's very unlikely that it will achieve anything major," he says.

articles.title: Malacañang on Romualdez's health: Give his doctors benefit of the doubt
articles.summary: Malacañang on Wednesday said physicians who are assessing the condition of former speaker and Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez should be given the benefit of the doubt amid his…

blocks.text: Published September 9, 2026 2:44pm

Malacañang on Wednesday said physicians who are assessing the condition of former speaker and Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez should be given the benefit of the doubt amid his reported health issues.

In a press briefing, Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Atty. Claire Castro expressed belief that Romualdez will not be able to escape and evade the plunder charges against him if he is in the hospital.

"Sa mga kritiko, hindi mawawala ang kritisismo. Pero hindi natin mapipigil ang mga doktor kung ano ang nakikita nilang health condition ng isang akusado. Hindi rin naman maipipilit ng PNP o ng pamunuan ng DILG na dalhin agad ang isang akusado na mayroong nasertipikahan na hindi pa nararapat na tanggalin or i-remove from the hospital," Castro said.

(For critics, criticisms will always be there. But we cannot stop doctors from seeing what they see as the health condition of an accused. Nor can the PNP or the DILG leadership force them to immediately bring an accused who has been certified as not yet eligible for removal from the hospital.)
"At kung nasa hospital naman po 'yan, hindi naman po siguro 'yan makakatakas," she added.
(If he's in the hospital, he probably won't be able to escape.)
Castro also emphasized that doctors would tell the truth regarding the health condition of a person.

"Wala po tayong masasabi kung ano 'yan. Nandiyan po 'yan sa pagtingin ng kanilang mga doktor at ang doktor naman ay dapat nagsasabi ng katotohanan. So we will just give them the benefit of the doubt," she said.
(We cannot say what that is. That is up to the assessment of the doctors and the doctors should tell the truth. So we will just give them the benefit of the doubt.)
Romualdez was confined at a private hospital in San Juan City when authorities served his arrest warrant there on Monday evening.
The Office of the Ombudsman filed a P7.4-billion plunder case against Romualdez, former Ako Bicol party-list Representative Zaldy Co, and several others in connection with the flood control scam.
It has also said it would "strongly oppose" Romualdez's motion seeking hospital detention. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Sunsilk brings a fresher commute to Cebu with Modern Jeep Takeover
articles.summary: Sunsilk is offering free rides on pink-wrapped modern jeepneys along two Cebu City routes through September 17, 2026, as part of its Modern Jeepney Takeover activation. Passengers on participating…

blocks.text: Sunsilk is offering free rides on pink-wrapped modern jeepneys along two Cebu City routes through September 17, 2026, as part of its Modern Jeepney Takeover activation. Passengers on participating jeepneys can also try the Sunsilk WonderMist Shine+Scent Duo onboard during the ride.
The Sunsilk Modern Jeepney Takeover is running until September 17, 2026, giving Cebu commuters more chances to spot and ride the pink modern jeepneys around the city.
The two routes covered are 10H, running from Bulacao to SM City Cebu via P. Del Rosario, and 10M, running from Bulacao to SM City Cebu via Colon Street.
A little hair care for the commute

Selected modern jeepneys along the two routes have been wrapped in Sunsilk branding and painted pink, making them visually distinct from regular vehicles on the same routes. Passengers board for free during the activation period, with Sunsilk covering the usual fare cost.

Onboard, passengers have the opportunity to try the Sunsilk WonderMist Shine+Scent Duo, a hair mist product designed to reduce frizz and leave hair with a scented finish. The duo brings together hair care and fragrance in a format that fits naturally into a busy day, perfect for Cebuano commuters navigating heat, humidity, and city traffic throughout the day.
Where to catch the Sunsilk Modern Jeepney Takeover
The activation can be experienced along these routes:

items: 10H: Bulacao to SM City Cebu via P. Del Rosario
10M: Bulacao to SM City Cebu via Colon Street

articles.title: SUV overtakes motorcycle, hits bicycle, kills boy, injures another
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A 10-year-old boy died, while his 8-year-old companion was injured after the bicycle they were riding on was hit by an SUV on the provincial road of Barangay Candugay, Barili…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A 10-year-old boy died, while his 8-year-old companion was injured after the bicycle they were riding on was hit by an SUV on the provincial road of Barangay Candugay, Barili town, on Tuesday noon, September 8.
Authorities said that the SUV involved was registered with the Municipality of Barili, and it was driven by the town’s registered driver.
The 37-year-old driver, a resident of Barangay Boloc-Boloc, Barili town, was detained at the Barili Police Station pending the filing of charges.
Initial investigation showed that the SUV was traveling from Barangay Candugay to Barili proper when it sideswiped the bicycle ridden by the two boys.
The SUV tried to overtake a speeding motorcycle but it sideswiped the bicycle of the kids — with the 10-year-old kid pedaling the bicycle — at the other side of the road.
The two victims were rushed to the hospital for treatment, but the 10-year-old boy was declared dead on arrival by the attending physician.
The other kid, the 8-year-old bicycle passenger was admitted to the hospital for treatment of his injuries.

articles.title: Reigning Miss Austria Lucia Sisic dead at 22
articles.summary: Austrian beauty queen Lucia Sisic, who had battled a heart valve defect since birth, has died. She was 22. Sisic’s death was confirmed through a statement shared by CEO Kerstin Rigger and Jörg…

blocks.text: Austrian beauty queen Lucia Sisic, who had battled a heart valve defect since birth, has died. She was 22.
Sisic’s death was confirmed through a statement shared by CEO Kerstin Rigger and Jörg Rigger of Mission Austria, the organization that manages the Miss Austria pageant.

“It is with great shock and deep sadness that we have learned of the passing of our Miss Austria 2024 Lucia Sisic. Lucia will be remembered as a wonderful young woman,” the pair said in German via the organization’s Instagram page on Tuesday, Sept. 8. “Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with her family, friends and everyone who was close to her at this difficult time.”
“Dear Lucia, you will always be a part of our Miss Austria family. Rest in peace,” the statement concluded.
The cause of death was not disclosed to the public.
View this post on Instagram A post shared by Mission Austria (@missionaustria_official)

According to several local news outlets including Austrian broadsheet Die Presse, Sisic had undergone several surgeries to treat her heart defect, with her most recent procedure taking place in late 2025. It remains unclear whether her heart condition was related to her death.
In a 2024 post, Sisic opened up about her condition as she thanked the medical team that saved her life since she was a kid.

“Thanks to the specialists and dedicated doctors who have always gone to great lengths to save my life time and time again, I have overcome many difficult moments and have been given the opportunity to live a fulfilling life,” she said in German.
“So far, I have only overcome a fraction of what still lies ahead of me. Nevertheless, I am proud that I did not give up, even though there were many reasons to do so,” she stated.
View this post on Instagram A post shared by Lucia (@luciasisic)
Sisic won the Miss Austria title in 2024. The national pageant has not held another edition since then, making her the reigning titleholder. /ra

articles.title: Tony Weeks returns to Philippines for Suganob-Nontshinga rematch
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A familiar figure from some of boxing’s biggest nights is making his return to the Philippines. Veteran American referee Tony Weeks will serve as the third man in the…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A familiar figure from some of boxing’s biggest nights is making his return to the Philippines.

Veteran American referee Tony Weeks will serve as the third man in the ring when Boholano boxer Regie Suganob and South Africa’s Sivenathi Nontshinga collide in their much-anticipated rematch for an IBF world light flyweight title eliminator on Saturday, September 12, at the Bohol Wisdom School in Tagbilaran City.
For Weeks, it will mark his first assignment in the Philippines in nearly 14 years.

The last time the renowned referee officiated a fight in the country was on October 20, 2012, when he handled the vacant WBO bantamweight title fight between Cebuano star AJ Banal and Thailand’s Pungluang Sor Singyu at the SM Mall of Asia Arena.

Weeks stopped the fight at 1:45 of the ninth round after Sor Singyu dropped Banal and the Filipino rose from the canvas but was still visibly dazed. Sor Singyu went on to capture the vacant world title.
Now, the highly respected Las Vegas-based referee returns to Philippine soil for another significant world-title pathway fight, this time in Bohol.

Weeks is no stranger to boxing’s biggest stages. He was the third man in the ring for the legendary 2005 lightweight unification bout between Diego Corrales and Jose Luis Castillo, widely regarded as one of the greatest fights in boxing history.

He has also officiated major fights involving Manny Pacquiao and Floyd Mayweather Jr., including Pacquiao’s 2008 victory over Oscar De La Hoya and Mayweather’s bouts against Juan Manuel Marquez, Miguel Cotto and Marcos Maidana.

Weeks has also worked championship bouts for major sanctioning bodies, including the IBF and WBA. In May this year, he was among the veteran officials who conducted a referees’ seminar during the IBF’s 41st annual convention in Vietnam, discussing referee mechanics, fouls, communication, fighter safety and the timing of stoppages.
His appointment adds another layer of prestige to what PMI Bohol Boxing Promotions hopes will be one of the biggest boxing events ever staged on the island.

PMI Bohol Boxing Promotions chief Atty. Floriezyl Echavez Podot told CDN Digital that preparations for Kumong Bol-Anon 26 were already 80 percent complete, with the promotion now waiting for the arrival of the IBF officials from abroad.

“In my assessment as of today, we are 80% prepared. Once the IBF officials from abroad arrive, we’ll be good to go. Sanctions secured, purse ready; it will be up to the boxers on the scale when weigh-in day comes,” Podot said.
Nontshinga and his team, including trainers Bernie Pailman and Colin Nathan, arrived in Bohol last Sunday, giving the South African camp a full week to acclimatize before fight night.
While the fighters have yet to cross paths ahead of the bout, the anticipation among Boholano boxing fans has already reached fever pitch.
“Ang mga fans lang diri ang hyped up. Pero ang mga boxers wala pa kay wala pa sila nagkakita,” Podot said.
(The fans here are already hyped up. But the boxers have not yet seen each other.)
The stakes are high for Suganob and Nontshinga.
The winner of their rematch will earn the mandatory challenger spot for the IBF world light flyweight championship and a shot at reigning champion Thanongsak Simsri of Thailand.
Simsri, however, is scheduled to defend his title against Filipino challenger Mark “Rasta Mac” Vicelles on September 26 in Japan.

With an IBF world-title opportunity hanging in the balance and a veteran referee like Weeks calling the action, Kumong Bol-Anon 26 is shaping up to be a particularly significant night for Philippine boxing and for Bohol.

articles.title: Xyriel Manabat, Sassa Gurl set early best actress race at CinePanalo 2026
articles.summary: Xyriel Manabat and Sassa Gurl are emerging as early names to watch in the Best Actress race at the 2026 CinePanalo Film Festival. Manabat stars in Mikko Baldoza’s “Stuck on You,” while Sassa Gurl…

blocks.text: Xyriel Manabat and Sassa Gurl are emerging as early names to watch in the Best Actress race at the 2026 CinePanalo Film Festival.
Manabat stars in Mikko Baldoza’s “Stuck on You,” while Sassa Gurl takes the lead in Rodina Singh’s “Multwoh (Patay na Patay sa ‘Yo).”
The two actresses arrive at the festival from different directions: Manabat brings years of acting experience, while Sassa Gurl enters the competition as a newcomer with growing momentum.

In “Stuck on You,” Manabat plays Sheryl Bunga, a heartbroken manicurista who accidentally gets involved in a deadly conspiracy after accepting a hitman’s job. Her situation becomes more complicated when she falls for a man, played by River Joseph, whom she may eventually have to kill.

Manabat is a former child actress who won FAMAS Best Child Actress for “Ang Tanging Ina Mo (Last na ‘To!)” and “A Mother’s Story.” She later took on more mature dramatic roles in projects such as “Dirty Linen” and “Senior High.”
Sassa Gurl, meanwhile, plays Marcel, a queer college student who dies before confessing their feelings to their longtime crush Miguel, played by Joao Constancia, in “Multwoh.”
Marcel returns as a ghost, but instead of seeking revenge, they have one unfinished mission: to finally tell Miguel “I love you.”
Following appearances in “The Entitled” and “Balota,” Sassa Gurl recently earned Breakthrough Actress of the Year at the 2026 Platinum Stallion National Media Awards for “Bar Boys: After School.”

articles.title: Tiafoe gives Michelsen a hug, shoulder to cry on after US Open win
articles.summary: NEW YORK — Frances Tiafoe knew Alex Michelsen needed a shoulder to cry on. So after handing his fellow American a crushing defeat in the US Open quarterfinals Tuesday, Tiafoe held Michelsen in a long…

blocks.text: Frances Tiafoe, of the United States, right, and Alex Michelsen, of the United States, embrace after Tiafoe won their match during the quarterfinal round of the U.S. Open tennis championships, Tuesday, Sept. 8, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Seth Wenig)
NEW YORK — Frances Tiafoe knew Alex Michelsen needed a shoulder to cry on.
So after handing his fellow American a crushing defeat in the US Open quarterfinals Tuesday, Tiafoe held Michelsen in a long embrace while the 22-year-old sobbed into his shoulder.

“I really like Alex. I really, really do, and I just wanted to come up there and just dap him up,” Tiafoe said. “I didn’t think it was going to be as long as it was, but I understand the moment. He was definitely crying on my shoulders. Yeah, we just had some words for each other, and that was it.”

Michelsen was playing in his first Grand Slam quarterfinal and was just a few points from winning it after taking the first two sets. The No. 11-seeded Tiafoe came back to win 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6 (10-6), starting his turnaround after Michelsen failed to serve out the match with a 5-4 lead in the third set.
Michelsen said he didn’t speak much when they met at the net.

“I was trying to keep it together and I didn’t do a good job of that,” Michelsen said. “He was saying a lot of nice personal things. ‘You’ll be there. When I’m older, you’re going to be here, and we’re going to play it again in this type of circumstance.’ All that good stuff. He’s a great guy for consoling me in that moment.”

This was the third pro match between the two, with Tiafoe winning both previous encounters. Michelsen said after his fourth-round victory that Tiafoe was an “unbelievable guy and a very good friend of mine,” and said similar after Tuesday’s defeat.
“I don’t think anyone else could have made me cry in that moment, to be honest,” Michelsen said.

Tiafoe is 28, one of the leaders of American men’s tennis and a fan favorite at the US Open, where he has reached his third semifinal. He said Sunday in looking ahead to the match that he had developed a good relationship with Michelsen.
Jessica Pegula said she watched the end of the match before she took the court for her quarterfinal victory over Emma Navarro.
“Just seeing Alex hug him at the end, I started crying in the locker room,” the No. 3-ranked American said. “It was so heartbreaking. My heart hurt so much.”
Michelsen left the court with a towel on his head, raising his arm to acknowledge the cheers from the crowd. Tiafoe told those fans what he thought of Michelsen’s performance.
“I mean, he easily could have won today so shout out to Alex Michelsen,” Tiafoe said.

articles.title: Malacañang leaves fate of possible VP Sara Duterte subpoena to Senate
articles.summary: Malacañang on Wednesday said that it is up to the Senate to decide if ever the House prosecution panel requests a subpoena to compel Vice President Sara Duterte to testify in her own impeachment…

blocks.text: Published September 9, 2026 2:15pm

Malacañang on Wednesday said that it is up to the Senate to decide if ever the House prosecution panel requests a subpoena to compel Vice President Sara Duterte to testify in her own impeachment trial.

Palace Press Officer Usec. Claire Castro said this in a press briefing, following the announcement of the prosecution on Tuesday that it intends to call Duterte to the witness stand to affirm and confirm her allegation of innocence.
“Kung ‘yan ang nais ng prosecution at kung papayagan po ito ng Senado, nasa kamay na po ito ng Senado,” Castro said.
(If that is what the prosecution wants and if the Senate allows it, then the matter rests with the Senate.)
“Hindi natin alam kung ito ang right timing for them. But muli, nasa Senado na ang pagpapasya tungkol diyan,” she added.
(We don’t know if this is the right timing for them. But again, the decision regarding that is up to the Senate.)
Castro also said that it was Duterte herself who said that she wants a bloodbath amid the allegations against her.

“Malamang kaya ito hinihiling ng prosecution ay dahil mismo naman ang Bise Presidente ang nagsabi na gusto niya ng isang bloodbath. At sinabi niya rin naman before handa siyang humarap patungkol dito at liwanagin ang mga isyu na ito,” the Palace official said.

(The prosecution is likely making this request because the Vice President herself said she wanted a bloodbath. She also previously stated that she was ready to face the allegations and clarify these issues.)

Asked if she thinks the Vice President will attend her own trial should a subpoena be issued, Castro said, “Kung psychologist ako o psychiatrist ako ng Bise Presidente…hindi ko masagot. Hypothetical question.”
(If I were the Vice President’s psychologist or psychiatrist... I couldn't answer that. It’s a hypothetical question.)
Impeachment court spokesperson Regie Tongol on Tuesday said oral arguments may be conducted if the prosecution panel requests a subpoena to compel Duterte to attend the trial. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Prosecution eyes around 25 witnesses on Sara Duterte's unexplained wealth
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel is eyeing to field 25 witnesses to prove Article 2 of the impeachment case against Vice President Sara Duterte which accuses the Vice President of accumulating unexplained…

blocks.text: Published September 9, 2026 2:06pm

The House prosecution panel is eyeing to field 25 witnesses to prove Article 2 of the impeachment case against Vice President Sara Duterte, which accuses her of accumulating unexplained wealth, Prosecutor Joel Chua of Manila said Wednesday.

“When I talked to Congressman Chel Diokno [of Akbayan] and Terry Ridon [of Bicol Saro party-list], they said they intend to present 10 witness, and that does not include bank officials yet,” Chua said in a press conference.

Chua said that is why the prosecution submitted a request for admission, which asks the Vice President to admit the authenticity and ownership of certain bank accounts that are subject of the case, including those accounts she shares with her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, since she has personal knowledge of these things.

“We asked for a stipulation because what I know is we will be fielding 15 bank officials [as witnesses]. If she will agree, our witnesses for this Article will be reduced by 10, more or less,” Chua added.

Aside from bank officials, Chua said among those lined up as witnesses for the prosecution are former Senator Antonio Trillanes IV, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla or any representative of the Ombudsman, as well as representatives from the Bureau of Internal Revenue, Securities and Exchange Commission and the Anti-Money Laundering Council.
“We’ll get a feel of it as we go along. If we feel that we already established our point, we can choose to rest our case just like in the other Articles of Impeachment,” Chua said.
The impeachment case alleges that the Vice President accumulated unexplained wealth through the following:

items: failure to fully and truthfully disclose all her and her spouse's assets, liabilities, and net worth in her statement of assets, liabilities, and net worth (SALN) including in her SALN for the years 2022, 2023, and 2024; and
failure to divest, and instead, willfully continued, all her business interests during her tenure as vice president for the years 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Casas' buzzer-beater completes CIT-U comeback over UP Cebu
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines – Axyl James Casas hit a game-winning shot from near midcourt with six seconds remaining as the Cebu Institute of Technology-University (CIT-U) Wildcats completed a stunning…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines – Axyl James Casas hit a game-winning shot from near midcourt with six seconds remaining as the Cebu Institute of Technology-University (CIT-U) Wildcats completed a stunning comeback against the University of the Philippines Cebu Fighting Maroons, 71-70, in the Cesafi Season 26 men’s basketball tournament Tuesday night at the Cebu Coliseum.
CIT-U overcame a 26-point deficit after UP Cebu took control early and led, 51-25, at halftime.
The Wildcats gradually worked their way back in the second half, cutting into the Fighting Maroons’ advantage in the third quarter before making their final push in the fourth.

UP Cebu remained in front, 70-68, in the closing seconds and appeared on course to secure the victory. But after the Fighting Maroons missed a crucial free throw, CIT-U secured the rebound and pushed the ball up the floor.
The Wildcats found Casas, who is from Ozamis City near midcourt, and he knocked down the long-range attempt to give CIT-U the lead for good.
John Rodulfa led the Wildcats with 15 points, while Braebon Thompson posted 14 points and 11 rebounds. Jerian Marc Abello contributed 11 points, while Casas finished with 10.
AJ delos Reyes led UP Cebu with 15 points and was the lone Fighting Maroon to score in double figures.
The victory improved CIT-U’s record to 2-0, putting the Wildcats on top of the standings, while UP Cebu dropped to 1-1.

articles.title: White Australia party is ‘modern manifestation’ of Nazi movement and should be banned, commonwealth tells high court
articles.summary: The former National Socialist Network is challenging ban in high court, arguing law breaches implied freedom of political communication

blocks.text: The White Australia party is a “modern manifestation” of Adolf Hitler’s Nazi movement and would motivate hate crimes against sections of the country, the high court has heard.

The White Australia party, formerly known as the National Socialist Network (NSN), was designated as an illegal hate group in May after the Australian Security and Intelligence Organisation (Asio) passed on its recommendation to the home affairs minister, Tony Burke.

It is challenging the ban at the high court over two days this week, with its lawyers arguing the law breaches the implied freedom of political communication and that handing the decision to Burke breaches the separation of powers.
It also argues the commonwealth does not have the power to ban political parties, citing a major cold war-era high court ruling in 1951, which overturned a ban on the Communist party of Australia.

The commonwealth’s lawyer, Brendan Lim, told the court on Wednesday the group sought to create a political party after anti-hate laws passed in the wake of the Bondi terror attack threatened to disband it.
The hate group listing means that supporting, funding, training, recruiting and joining the group constitutes a criminal offence with a maximum penalty of 15 years in prison.
Lim said the group sought “protection” under the guise of creating a political party but remained the same group with the same goals.

The barrister cited a series of examples, including inflammatory rhetoric to encourage communal violence, an alleged physically violent attack by some of its members on Camp Sovereignty in 2025, and past criminal convictions of its leader, Thomas Sewell.
Justice Robert Beech-Jones asked whether the commonwealth believed the group were the “modern manifestation” of Hitler’s Nazi movement. Lim responded: “Yes.”
“There are few legitimate reasons, outside of history books and museum, that warrant the use of Nazi symbols,” Lim said.

Citing a briefing from Asio and public speeches by its director general, Mike Burgess, Lim said the prohibited hate group listing was necessary because the group were security conscious and its operations savvy enough to work within the limits of the law.
“The existence of the group itself is the source of harm,” Lim said.
after newsletter promotion
Lim said stochastic terrorism – the use of media and public discourse to demonise sections of the community – could lead lone wolves or fringe members to commit racially motivated hate crimes.
Lim said the anti-hate laws go “no further than necessary” to remove that harm.
Lawyers for the party argued on Tuesday a total ban on the party was akin to using a “sledgehammer on a nut”.

Barrister Shahed Sharify argued the law’s breach of implied freedom of political communication was “authoritarian in nature” and suggested it could be used to outlaw any political party where its members had threatened or engaged in a hate crime with the assistance of the organisation.
Sharify said the banning of hate groups was determined by a politician, based on an opinion with no judicial fairness to appeal that decision.
Sharify said the law’s purposes would be better served by handing that decision to a judge rather than a “busy minister who flicks through a brief and decides in two hours”.

articles.title: 3 suspects in Degamo slay found guilty of illegal possession of gun, bombs
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines—A Manila court has found three former Army soldiers, who were earlier linked to the killing of former Negros Oriental Governor Roel Degamo, guilty of illegal possession of…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—A Manila court has found three former Army soldiers, who were earlier linked to the killing of former Negros Oriental Governor Roel Degamo, guilty of illegal possession of firearms and explosives.
Manila Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 40, in an Aug. 18 decision, convicted Joric Labrador of unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition.
It also found Joven Javier and Benjie Rodriguez guilty of one count each of unlawful possession of explosives in connection with the assassination of Degamo in March 2023.
Labrador was sentenced to up to 10 years in prison, while Javier and Rodriguez were meted a prison term of reclusion perpetua or 20 years.

The court also directed that the firearm and explosives seized from the three accused be handed over to the Philippine National Police.These items include a .45 caliber pistol, two magazines, 14 rounds of live ammunition, and two hand grenades,
The three respondents are also facing multiple murder and frustrated murder and attempted murder charges before the Manila RTC for the killing of Degamo.
The 56-year-old governor was shot down inside his home in Pamploma town, Negros Oriental.
According to the Department of Justice, which brought the charges to the Manila RTC, the validity of warrantless arrests was upheld in these cases.
This is because the confiscated items were properly identified and handled, based on testimonies by the police and other witnesses. /apl

articles.title: NPA leader killed in clash with Army troops in Leyte
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY- A ranking New People’s Army (NPA) leader was killed in a brief clash with government troops on Tuesday afternoon in the hinterlands of Barangay Caridad, Baybay City, Leyte, the…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY- A ranking New People’s Army (NPA) leader was killed in a brief clash with government troops on Tuesday afternoon in the hinterlands of Barangay Caridad, Baybay City, Leyte, the military reported.

The Army’s 8th Infantry Division(ID), which is based in Catbalogan City, Samar, said the encounter occurred on Sept. 8 after soldiers received information from a resident about the presence of armed men allegedly collecting money and food from communities in the area.
Troops from the 802nd Infantry Brigade(IB) proceeded to the area to verify the report, resulting in a firefight that lasted about five minutes, according to the military.
Killed was Erwin Murillo Maceda, alias “Romnick,” who was identified by the Army as the vice team leader of the NPA’s Island Committee Levox under the Eastern Visayas Regional Party Committee.
An M16 rifle was also recovered from the encounter site, the 8th ID said.

Brig. Gen. Pompeyo Jason Almagro, commander of the 802nd IB, said Maceda and his group had allegedly been involved in extortion, threats against residents and business owners, and attacks on government security installations in Leyte.

“The people of Leyte have endured years of fear, intimidation, and disruption caused by armed groups. We will not allow these conditions to return to communities that have worked hard to achieve peace,” Almagro said in a statement released on Wednesday.

The military said the encounter followed reports of armed NPA members attempting to regain their presence in communities where government authorities have declared stable peace and security conditions.
The Army also credited residents’ cooperation and timely reporting for enabling government forces to respond to the reported presence of armed men.
“The cooperation of our communities is critical. Their timely reporting allows government forces to respond before threats can escalate,” Almagro said.
The 8th ID renewed its call for remaining NPA members to abandon armed struggle and surrender, saying government programs are available to assist former rebels who return to civilian life.
The military said it would continue operations in areas where armed groups are reported to be operating while encouraging NPA members to return peacefully to their families and communities./coa

articles.title: P1.79-M shabu confiscated from high-value suspects in Taguig, Valenzuela
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Police on Wednesday confiscated suspected shabu or methamphetamine hydrochloride with a combined value of P1.79 million, and arrested five suspects during separate…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Police on Wednesday confiscated suspected shabu or methamphetamine hydrochloride with a combined value of P1.79 million, and arrested five suspects during separate buy-bust operations in Taguig and Valenzuela cities.
The confiscated substances had a combined weight of 263.6 grams, the National Capital Region Police Office said.
According to law enforcement, the arrest happened after an undercover police officer purchased alleged shabu from a 37-year-old newly identified high-value suspect.
Police also arrested his other accomplices, including two newly identified high-value individuals aged 35 and 20, and a 28-year-old high-value individual.
Seized during the operation were six heated-sealed plastic sachets of suspected shabu, a mobile phone, and other personal items.

The authorities also confiscated a Glock 14 Gen 5 pistol with one magazine and seven rounds of live ammunition from the 37-year-old suspect, facing another charge aside from drug trafficking for violating the Republic Act No. 10591, or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act.
The four suspects arrested in Taguig were taken into police custody and are expected to face charges for violations of the Republic Act No. 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002.
The seized drugs and other evidence will be subjected to forensic examination.
Anotherbuy-bust operation in Barangay Punturin, Valenzuela City, at 4:49 a.m. resulted in the arrest of a 45-year-old high-value individual and the confiscation of P432,480 worth of alleged shabu.
Authorities recovered two plastic sachets allegedly containing 63.6 grams of suspected shabu.
Under police custody, the suspect faces charges of violating Sections 5 and 11 of Republic Act No. 9165 and will be referred to the City Prosecutor’s Office for inquest proceedings.

NCR Officer-in-ChargePolice Brig. Gen. Christopher Abrahano said that the back-to-back operations show the NCRPO’s efforts to disrupt illegal drug activities and prevent firearms from being used in further criminal acts.

“We will continue to focus our operations on high‑value individuals and areas being used for illegal drug activities. The recovery of a firearm in one of these operations further underscores the need for sustained, intelligence‑driven police actions to prevent more serious crimes and protect our communities,” Abrahano said in a statement. Martina Nieyandra Calica. Inquirer.net trainee /mr

articles.title: Mimaropa cops plant over 31,000 trees under environmental project
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Police planted 31,592 trees across the Mimaropa region since launching an environmental initiative in July, the regional police office said in a statement on…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Police planted 31,592 trees across the Mimaropa region since launching an environmental initiative in July, the regional police office said in a statement on Wednesday.

The latest tree-planting activity was held on Sept. 8 in Barangay Sta. Isabel, Pinamalayan town in Oriental Mindoro, where nearly 300 participants planted more than 100 narra seedlings and over 100 fruit-bearing trees.

Oriental Mindoro Police Provincial Office (ORMIN PPO) led the activity, bringing together police personnel, firefighters, local government representatives, civic organizations, and other community partners.

Brig. Gen. Christopher Dela Cruz, MIMAROPA police director, joined the activity and said environmental protection forms part of the police’s broader responsibility to help build safe and resilient communities.
“Hindi lamang tayo nagtipon para magtanim ng puno. Nandito tayo upang magtanim ng pag-asa, malasakit, at pananagutan para sa kinabukasan,” Dela Cruz said.
(We did not just gather to plant trees. We are here to plant hope, compassion, and accountability for the future.)

The police regreening initiative, called Project T.R.E.E. (Take Responsibility for the Enhancement of the Environment), was launched on July 6 as part of Dela Cruz’s F.I.G.H.T. C.R.I.M.E.S. framework./coa

articles.title: Alleged victim of Alan Jones looked ‘sunken and diminished’, politician tells court
articles.summary:
Downing Centre court hears that the alleged victim was usually outgoing but his demeanour changed at a meeting with Jones at his apartment

• Listen to the podcast

blocks.text: A politician who worked with an alleged victim of Alan Jones has told a Sydney court the man looked uncharacteristically “sunken and diminished” when meeting with the broadcaster at his Circular Quay apartment.

The former MP, who Guardian Australia has chosen not to name because it may lead to the identification of the alleged victim, known as complainant C, said the man was usually outgoing and engaged but his demeanour changed once he sat down at a table with his former boss.
The court heard C, who was Jones’s driver as a young man, was “anxious and uncomfortable” when the three men sat at a rectangular table for a meeting in Jones’s waterfront property.
C had gone on to work for a politician after leaving Jones, and he accompanied his boss to a meeting with Jones about a board role.
The witness said C did not speak and did not make eye contact which was highly unusual for someone who usually had a lot to contribute.

In his evidence-in-chief last month C said the meeting at the Toaster left him anxious and uncomfortable. He was challenged by the defence because he had sent Jones a text at the time saying how much he enjoyed seeing him.
Earlier on Thursday, the court heard from multiple friends and colleagues who testified that C told them that as a young man he was indecently assaulted by the broadcaster.
The second alleged victim to give evidence at the trial, C has said that over the years he had mentioned to people in his life that he had been touched inappropriately by Jones.
Jones has pleaded not guilty to 20 charges of indecent assault and two counts of sexual touching against six complainants.
In a day of rapid fire evidence, the Downing Centre court heard from six people who said that C would sporadically confide in them how his then-boss would touch him inappropriately.
A former colleague who worked with C in a government role said one day he was driving with C along the Hume Highway when he made an allegation about his time working as a driver for Jones.
“We were talking about 2GB and he was reminiscing about driving Mr Jones around and he communicated that [Jones] had reached into his crotch and squeezed it,” the witness said.
Asked by the prosecution how he responded, the witness apologised to the court for using crude language and said he answered “What the fuck?”.
“And C said ‘that’s just Alan, that’s his behaviour’,” he told the court, adding that C said Jones was “a very powerful man within 2GB”.
C’s father-in-law did not give evidence but his police statement was read out in court.

He said his son-in law occasionally told anecdotes about working for Jones, including one occasion when Jones invited him into his Circular Quay apartment and “when Alan sat down in his chair he was only wearing a dressing gown with nothing underneath” and C said “his undercarriage was hanging out”.
His father-in-law told police that C in 2023 disclosed to him that Jones had “pushed him up against the wall and kissed me” and he had “not previously told me about the hurt it caused”.
Another witness, a school friend, told the court C alleged that Jones would say inappropriate things about genitals in text messages to him.

Another colleague told the court that when C was at his house and they were watching horse racing, C commented on a presenter on Sky Racing “who was dressed very flamboyantly” and C asked “do you want to know if he is gay’”?
The witness said yes he did and C replied: “He said he was ‘as gay as Alan grabbing me on the cock day’”.

Another pupil at the same school who became friends with C as an adult said he would make reference to things that happened to him while working for Jones, like “being grabbed on the cock” and “that he would be kissed”.
Another colleague, who worked with C for a politician, said C said: In the office “he said when he drove Mr Jones he would put his hand on his leg and go the grope”.

Another former school mate who later became a colleague said at a lunch with friends C adopted a joking tone and said: “Did anything happen with you when you were working with Alan? He tried to kiss me in the lift once. And I said what do you mean?” They never discussed it again.
The trial before judge Glenn Walsh continues.

articles.title: Reform UK says migrant deal was ratified by far-right National Rally president
articles.summary:
Agreement between Nigel Farage and Jordan Bardella to return migrants to France faces backlash, with critics saying it goes against France’s ‘interests and sovereignty’

Reform UK has…
articles.byline: Rowena Mason and Angelique Chrisafis in Paris

blocks.text: Reform UK has insisted its deal with France’s far-right National Rally to return migrants back across the channel was fully approved by the party and signed off by its president, Jordan Bardella, amid a furious backlash in France.

The agreement unveiled on Friday between Nigel Farage and Bardella, who is the 30-year-old protege of presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, appeared to directly contradict Le Pen’s long-held policy of refusing to accept the return of those who arrive in the UK in small boats from France.

Le Pen was pressed for her position by journalists from France TV, the state broadcaster, on Monday. Le Pen declined to comment, saying she would talk about the issue soon, but at a time of her choosing.
In 2021, Le Pen said she wanted a rewriting of border agreements for the UK to specifically send people arriving on boats back to their countries of origin, instead of returning them to France.

Since the agreement, Bardella has come under fire from political parties in France for signing the deal, with Benjamin Haddad, the Europe minister, criticising Bardella for “submission” that was “against our interests and sovereignty”.

Some French media have questioned whether Bardella was duped by Reform, querying whether the French translation accurately conveyed the meaning by Farage that the National Rally (RN) was prepared to accept any migrants back who travel by small boat.

However, a Reform spokesperson said it was “signed off by both Bardella and the presidential team”, that the policy was included in the French version as well as the English, and it could “confirm both parties are fully on board”.

Until the summer, Bardella had been considered as a potential replacement for Le Pen in next spring’s presidential election but will now run as her future prime minister. In July, when a Paris appeal court upheld Le Pen’s conviction for embezzling European parliament funds, her ban from running for office was reduced, allowing her to stand.
Farage has kept Le Pen at arm’s length, while having cultivated good relations with Bardella over the past year, but he is rumoured to be planning to meet her later in the autumn.

He previously rejected the idea of a tie-up in 2014 in the European parliament when he accused Le Pen’s party of having a history of “prejudice and antisemitism”, which she said was slander. Last week, Farage said he would not have done a deal with the party when led by Jean-Marie Le Pen, Marine’s father, a convicted Holocaust denier who co-founded the Front National in 1972. Le Pen expelled her father from the party in 2015. Farage praised her, saying she had got rid of “extreme elements”.
At the heart of the row in France is the wording of the document Farage brought out for Bardella to sign with him on stage in Birmingham, calling it a memorandum of understanding.

Both texts, presented side by side in English and French, state that, if Farage and Bardella become prime ministers of their respective countries, the UK will intercept boats launched from the French coast, and that France will return people onboard to their countries of origin.

But the English text carried an extra phrase saying “France will ordinarily accept these persons” who would then be returned to their home country. This appeared to show that Bardella was promising to accept returned persons in France, which contradicts the long-held position of RN.

France TV said RN denied any controversy, saying the text was only a declaration of intention that would be refined at a later point. Speaking in Italy over the weekend, Bardella suggested his party in government would prevent migrants from reaching France by much tougher border controls, resulting in the numbers crossing to the UK being much lower.
However, RN’s opponents were critical of Bardella for signing a memorandum on immigration on stage with Farage.

The MP, Sacha Houlié, an ally of the centre-left would-be presidential candidate, Raphael Glucksmann, wrote on X about what he called “a miserable episode where the whole of France could see Mr Bardella used as a doormat by the English far-right.” He told the RN: “You claim to be patriots, you’re cowards.”

Gabriel Attal, the former centrist prime minister and presidential candidate, wrote on X: “To applause from his party members, Nigel Farage made Jordan Bardella sign a memorandum to ensure that all migrants intercepted in the Channel are sent back to France. Either Jordan Bardella doesn’t understand English or he is shamefully weak when it comes to defending French interests. And I think he does understand English.”

Édouard Philippe, a former prime minister and centre-right candidate, said it was an example of hypocrisy and division in Bardella’s party. Philippe said it looked like Bardella found it difficult to stand up to Farage in order to “protect French interests”.

Xavier Bertrand, the rightwing head of the northern Hauts-de-France region, wrote on X that in agreeing that France alone would take responsibility for returning people to their home countries, Bardella was “reducing France to the status of Britain’s subcontractor.”

Chris Philp, the Conservative shadow home secretary, said: “Reform UK’s deal with Jordan Bardella is a complete farce … Time and again, Reform prove they are fundamentally unserious with grand claims for the cameras, with none of the detail or hard work that might survive actual scrutiny.”

articles.title: Apple expected to unveil folding iPhone as new CEO takes center stage
articles.summary:
The new model will serve as the first big test for John Ternus, who took the role last week

All eyes are on Apple’s annual fall announcement of new products this afternoon, where the company…

blocks.text: All eyes are on Apple’s annual fall announcement of new products this afternoon, where the company is expected to unveil the most significant change to the iPhone since the smartphone’s introduction in 2007.
Unlike previous iterations, the new iPhone is expected to fold, opening and closing like a passport to double its screen size.
The product release event, titled “Surprise and Shine”, begins at 10am Pacific Standard Time on Apple’s campus in Cupertino, California, south of San Francisco.

While competitors have released foldable smartphones since the late 2010s, the new model will be a first for the iPhone maker and will also serve as the first big test for the company’s new CEO, John Ternus, who assumed the role on 1 September.

Apple is expected to price the phone north of $2000, more than what some of its competitors charge for their foldable phones. A Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold, for instance, retails for $1899. Much remains unknown about Apple’s device, including its name, though it is rumored to be named either the iPhone Fold or the iPhone Ultra.

Apple reportedly began testing prototypes of its folding iPhone display in early 2021 – though at the time there were no plans for its launch, according to a Bloomberg report. Ultimately, the phone the company is rumored to launch will be about 5.5in when it’s closed and 7.8in when it opens. It’s also not expected to have Face ID because the device is too thin to hold the camera that would enable the facial recognition scan. Reports indicate it will only offer Touch ID instead.

Apple is also expected to make several more routine announcements, including new iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max models. Though the foldable iPhone may take center stage Wednesday, demand for foldable phones makes up only a small sliver of overall mobile device sales. Customers’ interest in standard iPhones, by contrast, remains high, as evidenced in Apple’s most recent robust earnings.

The company is also expected to unveil new iterations of some of its other product offerings at its events and over the next few months, including updates to its Apple Watch and AirPods lines, according to Bloomberg, as well as its first-ever touchscreen MacBook.

Ternus will take the stage as CEO for the first time and mark the beginning of his tenure as the head of Apple, replacing outgoing CEO Tim Cook. In a note to employees on his first day, Ternus said that he was excited about “the incredible products already in the works and the ones we haven’t even imagined”.
after newsletter promotion

“I’m honored to be stepping into this role at what is truly the greatest company in the world, and I am so excited about everything we have in store,” Ternus wrote in his letter. “We have a huge launch next week that’s going to be phenomenal. Thanks for everything you’ve all done to make it possible.”

articles.title: Polanski calls for report on ecosystem collapse to be published in full
articles.summary:
Green leader says ministers must stop ‘hiding the truth’ about threat to UK security from climate and nature crisis

Zack Polanski will challenge Andy Burnham’s government to publish an…

blocks.text: Zack Polanski will challenge Andy Burnham’s government to publish an unredacted version of an explosive report by the UK’s spy chiefs that found the collapse of overseas ecosystems would have catastrophic consequences for the UK’s national security.

The Green party leader in England will demand that the prime minister come clean about the scale and impact of the climate and nature crisis and call on the government to publish in full the report that warns the UK faces devastating security consequences.

Speaking at the Wild Summit event in Bristol on Wednesday, Polanski will ask the prime minister: “Will you tell the truth – and release the full unredacted report from the joint intelligence chiefs? Or will you keep hiding the truth from the public?”

The Guardian revealed last year that the report paints a devastating picture of severe food shortages, price rises, migration, political destabilisation and possible war, resulting from the collapse of ecosystems, fuelled by the human-induced climate crisis and over-exploitation.

A redacted 14-page version, including some of the report’s findings, was published in January but the government has repeatedly refused to publish the full version, despite repeated freedom of information requests from journalists and calls from MPs.

Polanski, who is expected to be the Green party candidate in the upcoming byelection in Holborn and St Pancras, will argue that the extreme weather experienced by much of the UK this summer should be a wake-up call for ministers.

“It was a bleak preview of what is to come if we continue to allow the greed of corporations to come above the survival of our natural world – and all that relies on it. This must mark a turning point. Where we say: no more loss, no more quieting of birdsong, no more steady trickling of sewage and poison into our waters.”

The report by the joint intelligence committee and other government departments, revealed by the Guardian last October, shows that the UK will face catastrophic consequences from the collapse of key ecosystems in other countries. These include the Amazon rainforest, which scientists fear is reaching a “tipping point” triggered by deforestation and rising temperatures, which would turn the ecosystem from a huge absorber of carbon dioxide into a net source of carbon.

Food shortages would be almost certain to result from the decline of ecosystems overseas, the report found, as would a big increase in global migration, with the potential to fuel unrest. Among the most alarming findings was that armed conflict, which includes nuclear war, was also a potential consequence.

The report was due to be published at an event last October, attended by King Charles, in the Natural History Museum. However, at the last minute the publication was pulled, at the behest of Downing Street.
Simultaneously, in a letter to Burnham, a coalition of green groups has warned that national security, public health and economic growth are at risk without urgent action to restore nature.

The UK has a legally binding target to restore 30% of nature by 2030. This target, which was set by more than 100 countries during Cop15 negotiations in Montreal in 2022, is considered the minimum restoration needed to halt and reverse the global decline in nature. The UK is currently on track to miss this target, with a recent plan to reach this target in England condemned as “pathetic” and “completely insufficient”.
after newsletter promotion

“Your government has diplomatic and legal obligations to halt the decline of wildlife and protect 30% of the land and sea for nature by 2030 … On the current path the UK will miss those targets,” the groups warn the prime minister in the letter.

The letter also highlights that two-thirds of the UK’s protected nature sites need “urgent repair”, with many of these sites neglected or damaged by intensive industry, pollution and the climate crisis. The groups warn this leaves communities and businesses exposed to flooding, drought, wildfires and pollution. This warning comes as new research finds that around £2bn a year needs to be invested in protected nature sites – up from roughly £1.1bn today – to restore them by 2042. The groups are calling for more funding, stronger laws and decisive enforcement to “stop the abuses that are hollowing out our natural world”.
A Labour spokesperson said: “This is the first government to take seriously the risks that climate change and nature loss pose to our food security, economic resilience, and national security.

“We’re taking decisive action, including launching the UK’s first taskforce on the national security and resilience risks of climate change and nature loss, investing in nature recovery at home and abroad, and delivering the largest nature-friendly farming budget in history.”

articles.title: UK datacentres will create just 25% of jobs predicted by tech sector, analysis finds
articles.summary:
Facilities likely to employ 10,400 workers, compared with 40,000 in industry estimates, thinktank says

Datacentres in the UK will create just a quarter of the jobs predicted by the tech…

blocks.text: Datacentres in the UK will create just a quarter of the jobs predicted by the tech sector, while consuming vast amounts of energy, according to new research.

Environmental thinktank Verdant predicts that all the datacentres currently planned are likely to directly employ 10,400 workers – compared with the more than 40,000 cited in projections by the industry lobby group TechUK.

Labour has defended the rapid rollout of AI datacentres in the face of growing public scepticism, amid concerns about their demand for water and energy. The government has also echoed TechUK’s claims about job creation.

Verdant’s analysis is based on 20 projects for which data on staffing levels are publicly available, including via planning applications, company accounts and press releases – as well as international comparisons.

It says the datacentres that have already been built have directly created fewer than 4,400 jobs – about 8.6 jobs for each megawatt of energy they consume, against the 43.7 jobs claimed in TechUK’s projections.

Verdant also argues that the many future projects currently at the planning stage are on a far larger scale, and so likely to be much less job-intensive – perhaps creating as few as 1.6 permanent positions per megawatt.
Its analysis focuses on the permanent workers needed to maintain and operate datacentres, setting aside the much larger number of temporary construction jobs needed to build them.
James Meadway, the thinktank’s co-director, said: “We’re being rushed into supporting a frantic pace of datacentre buildout on very flimsy economic grounds.

“Clearly artificial intelligence and related technologies have great potential. But vast new datacentres arrive at significant real costs to local communities and even our climate ambitions, and their use case has to be made by the government and industry – rather than assuming we can build first and then work out why we did later.”

blocks.caption: Demonstrators protest against redevelopment plans for the 10-acre Truman Brewery site in Brick Lane, which include a datacentre. Photograph: Carlos Jasso/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: To underline the resource intensity of the vast data warehouses, Verdant compared the 8.6 jobs they currently create per megawatt of power used with about 400 in a car plant and more than 3,600 in a hospital or health facility.

The government rejected this comparison, and questioned Verdant’s methodology. A spokesperson said: “This report relies on a deeply misleading jobs-per-megawatt metric, makes false comparisons with hospitals and schools, and appears to confuse electricity capacity with actual consumption. More seriously, it discounts the wider economic value of compute [computing capacity] and the national security and sovereignty case for building critical digital infrastructure in Britain.”

Verdant said it had based its calculations on the electricity capacity that tech firms claim they need – which could still crowd out alternative plans, even if the completed datacentres don’t end up using all the capacity.

Labour has classified AI datacentres as critical national infrastructure in an attempt to speed up the planning process, and Andy Burnham has underlined his backing for the sector by appointing AI minister Kanishka Narayan to his cabinet.
after newsletter promotion

Narayan has advocated a rapid increase in datacentres, partly on grounds of national sovereignty. He told the Times last month: “The British public is very clear that it wants strong defence. It wants strong, sovereign capability, it doesn’t just want foreign billionaires to own things that matter to our lives. If we’re being true to those British values, it is impossible to achieve that without building a sovereign level of datacentre capacity in this country.”
By contrast, the Green party in England has called for a moratorium on building datacentres, while there have been protests in Scotland, amid claims that massive projects are being rushed through.

Zack Polanski, the party’s leader in England, said: “The government is planning to steamroller local opposition so private companies can build datacentres – but it can’t explain what the benefits are.

‘“England and Wales are still facing drought after our hottest summer ever, but these datacentres are set to be given priority access to water. Meanwhile, this latest research suggests far fewer jobs may actually be created in constructing and staffing them than the government claims.”

In response to the Green party’s call for a “pause”, a government spokesperson insisted that it would “simply send investment and good jobs abroad, while leaving Britain dependent on overseas computing for the processing of sensitive health and defence data”.

A spokesperson for TechUK said: “Our estimates that the UK datacentre industry supports 43,500 jobs, and could support 40,000 more by 2035, are built on a published methodology using industry data and standard economic impact assessment techniques. The figures were built transparently from the best available industry data at the time, and we are confident they remain a reasonable estimate of the sector’s employment contribution.”
