articles.title: Ukraine’s prosecutor general quits after anti-corruption agents raid his office
articles.summary:
Ruslan Kravchenko resigns over allegations some of his officials were engaged in large-scale money laundering

Ukraine’s prosecutor general has resigned after investigators used ladders to…
articles.byline: Luke Harding in London and Amy Hawkins in Kharkiv

blocks.text: Ukraine’s prosecutor general has resigned after investigators used ladders to raid his office in connection with a major corruption scandal that threatens to embarrass Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Ruslan Kravchenko quit his post on Monday after allegations that some of his officials were involved in large-scale money laundering. They received cash to protect call centres involved in illegal phone scams, it was claimed.

Kravchenko, who denies wrongdoing, left his job after meeting Zelenskyy. Ukraine’s president also spoke to the heads of Nabu and Sapo, the two anti-corruption agencies that have uncovered a sprawling criminal scheme involving government officials.

Zelenskyy described his conversation with Kravchenko as “fairly long” and said: “I’m sure you understand what we discussed.” The prosecutor’s resignation letter will be sent to Ukraine’s parliament, the Verkhovna Rada, he said.

Kravchenko is the latest member of Zelenskyy’s inner circle to be linked to corruption. The allegations involve so-called call centres operating in Ukraine. Employees pose as banks, law enforcement agencies or investment advisers, and persuade victims to transfer funds to accounts or crypto wallets under their control.

Those targeted include Ukrainians, Russians and EU citizens. According to Nabu, a senior official inside the prosecutor general’s office protected the criminal network and helped it to launder its assets.

Each “call centre” paid $7,000 (£5,200) a month in protection money, law enforcement sources told the Ukrainska Pravda newspaper. The bribes ran into millions of dollars, it said, with hundreds of centres believed to employ about 60,000 people across the country.

Nabu investigators raided Kravchenko’s office on Friday. Staff refused to let them in so they used ladders to scale a metal gate. Kravchenko was not at work and had disappeared from his home, which was searched later that evening.

The chief suspect was arrested in the western city of Lviv. Recordings of phone calls published by Nabu suggested he was overseeing repairs at Kravchenko’s home while simultaneously collecting bribes from the fraudulent call centres.

Nabu released images over the weekend of a safe filled with bundles of dollar bills. It said it had uncovered five officials behind the scheme but did not name them. The cash was spent on real estate, jewellery and other valuables, it said, laying out its evidence in a 30-minute video.

Zelenskyy tried to strip Nabu and Sapo of their independence last year, a move he reversed after protests in Kyiv and other cities. There are further claims that the prosecutor’s office subsequently spied on Nabu staff and tried to obstruct their work.

The revelations come at a time when Ukraine is under day-and-night attack from Russian drones and missiles. Three people were killed and 19 injured in overnight strikes on Kyiv that caused huge fires and left smoke hanging over the city.

The onslaught marked the end of a three-day ceasefire in the capital after a visit on Sunday by Donald Trump’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. They visited Moscow on Saturday and met Vladimir Putin.

Zelenskyy said the pair had brought some “very good, worthwhile ideas” for ending the war but gave no further details. He said he hoped to meet Trump in the next two weeks. Few expect a breakthrough, with the Kremlin claiming on Tuesday that its forces were close to victory.
While Russia escalated its bombing, Ukrainians were talking about corruption investigations, posting numerous comments on social media, the transparency advocate Olena Tregub said.
after newsletter promotion

“Society is shocked and appalled by government officials who are basically behaving as mafia,” she said. “It’s not even corruption. It’s organised crime, protecting illegal call centres that were scamming people, not only in Ukraine but in Europe.”
She said anti-corruption investigations were different from previous ones because Nabu detectives were “very good technically”.

“They are recording people in their homes, in their offices and over the phone,” she said. “They are outsmarting other law enforcement bodies fighting against them, and are able to tape people who think everything is discreet.”
She said the high-profile raids were “changing the culture in Ukraine” and making society less tolerant of ill-gotten wealth.

Zelenskyy’s former business partner fled the country last year after being implicated in a corruption case featuring the state nuclear energy company. Two ministers were fired. The president’s powerful chief of staff, Andriy Yermak, also later resigned after being questioned. Both deny wrongdoing.
Kravchenko rejected the allegations against him on Sunday, calling them “completely unsubstantiated”. A day later he said he did not want his office “to be used as a tool in political confrontation”.

The deputy chair of parliament’s law enforcement committee, Andriy Osadchuk, said the ​scandal underlined the need to ‌reform the prosecution service ​and called for key posts ​to be filled through open competition. Fighting corruption was also vital to Kyiv’s bid for EU membership, he said.
“It will be very difficult for Ukraine to move forward if we do not change the approach to selecting and appointing the prosecutor general and prosecutors at lower levels,” Osadchuk said.

articles.title: Sandiganbayan summons Cardinal Santos doctors
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan Third Division has ordered four doctors of former House speaker Martin Romualdez to testify on his medical condition as it studies whether to let him remain in hospital confinement…

blocks.text: September 9, 2026 | 1:00am
DILG seeks Romualdez transfer to PNP hospital

MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Third Division has ordered four doctors of former House speaker Martin Romualdez to testify on his medical condition as it studies whether to let him remain in hospital confinement under custody.
The anti-graft court ordered doctors Rody Dy, Rogelio Libarnes, Kurt Allen Sibayan and Rosalio Torres to testify at a hearing set on Sept. 10.
Romualdez was also directed to appear before the court “should (his) condition permit.”
He and his doctors were ordered to present the results of all medical examinations the Leyte representative took during his hospital stay.

The court will hear the motion filed by Romualdez seeking continued hospital confinement at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center (CSMC) in San Juan where he checked in on Monday, about an hour after the warrant for his arrest was issued, after supposedly suffering a “cardiovascular event” and “anxiety attack.”

His medical certificate says he suffers from hypertensive atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, unstable angina, coronary artery disease, cerebrovascular ischemic disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia and primary hypothyroidism.
He also reportedly underwent angioplasty surgery in October 2024 due to a coronary artery disease and has since required continuing cardiac monitoring and treatment.
He claimed that he was confined at the same hospital in July this year as irregularities were found in his MRI scan examination.
The Sandiganbayan, however, emphasized that custody of Romualdez belongs to the anti-graft court.
Hospital transfer

Saying they oppose Romualdez’s continued stay at the San Juan hospital, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla pushed for the transfer of the 62-year-old lawmaker to the Philippine National Police General Hospital.

Remulla said the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG), which has custody of Romualdez, will file a motion to the Sandiganbayan Third Division to allow them to move Romualdez to the PNPGH at Camp Crame in Quezon City.
“That will be our initial step under formal custody. We will give him visitation and practicing rights, including his doctors,” he said at a news briefing.
Members of Romualdez’s immediate family and his lawyers are also allowed access to the former speaker, who was placed under arrest on Monday night after the anti-graft court ordered his arrest.

Remulla said the PNPGH is more capable to handle the condition of Romualdez, who suffered a transient ischemic attack in July 2026. The lawmaker also has an unstable blood pressure, with his latest BP at 148/82.
Remulla has ordered officials of the New Quezon City Jail along Payatas Road to prepare for Romualdez’s arrival when news broke that he was at the hospital.

Police have tightened security at the hospital as Remulla described Romualdez as a flight risk due to the resources at his disposal to evade arrest, such as two private jets, three helicopters and three yachts.
Remulla said he has yet to talk with President Marcos about Romualdez, who is the Chief Executive’s cousin.
“If you think it’s easy for the President, it’s not. There are no instructions from the President regarding the treatment,” he added.
Remulla said he and his brother, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla, are close friends with Romualdez.
“I told him, ‘I hope you understand why I’m doing this and it’s nothing personal,’ and he said ‘it’s OK, I understand’,” Remulla said.
Arrest warrant returned
The CIDG has returned to the Sandiganbayan the warrant of arrest against Romualdez, along with his medical evaluation from the CSMC.
CIDG National Capital Region chief Col. John Guiagui brought the documents to the anti-graft court’s Third Division, which is handling the plunder case.

He said Romualdez completed the booking procedures, including fingerprint scanning and mugshot taking. He said the lawmaker was already at the hospital before the warrant of arrest was issued by the court.
No special treatment
Romualdez was not accorded special treatment when he was placed under arrest on Monday night, the Philippine National Police said yesterday.
PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said they followed legal procedures in enforcing the arrest warrant issued by the Sandiganbayan against Romualdez.

Meanwhile, the National Bureau of Investigation has formed a special action unit to serve the arrest warrants against Romualdez’s co-accused in the plunder case, according to NBI Director Melvin Matibag. Matibag said the NBI received copies of the warrants on Monday night and immediately tasked its special action unit and Special Task Group with enforcing them. The warrants cover three other respondents, including former lawmaker Zaldy Co, Joselyn Serenio and Felicito Guevarra.
He said the NBI has coordinated with the Bureau of Immigration to determine whether Serenio and Guevarra have left the country.
Hospital arrest

In seeking hospital arrest, Romualdez filed a nine-page “manifestation of hospital confinement and urgent motion ad cautelam for continued hospital confinement under custody” before the Sandiganbayan.

“The certificate explains why the required care cannot, at this time, be safely delivered at a detention facility hospital, much less a detention facility, and identifies the clinical milestones or conditions upon which accused (Romualdez) may be medically cleared for transfers,” said Romualdez in the pleading obtained by reporters.
The hospital records also indicated that Romualdez had previously undergone a percutaneous coronary intervention, a procedure used to restore blood flow through a blocked coronary artery.
The medical certificate did not indicate a discharge date.- Emmanuel Tupas, Ghio Ong, Mark Ernest Villeza

articles.title: BARMM 2026 Elections: History, key dates, candidates, and everything you need to know
articles.summary: The historic first regular elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) are set to take place on September 14, 2026.

blocks.text: For generations, the story of the Bangsamoro has been shaped by a struggle for self-determination, marked by armed conflict, displacement, peace negotiations, and repeated attempts to establish meaningful autonomy in the southern Philippines.
On September 14, 2026, that long history will enter a new chapter.

The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) is set to hold its first parliamentary elections, allowing voters to choose the representatives who will form the region’s first elected parliament.

blocks.caption: 2026 BARMM Parliamentary Elections

blocks.text: The election marks a major step in the transition from an interim government through the Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA) to an elected regional administration.
President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. described it as the “fruition of an entire peace process that began in 1968, then the Tripoli Agreement, and then the BARMM.”
The elections are also a crucial test of whether the decades of peace efforts can be translated into a stable and democratic self-government.
However, the significance of the election cannot be understood without looking back at the history that led to the establishment of the BARMM.
Decades of struggle

The Bangsamoro homeland has a long history that existed even before the Philippines became an independent country. Muslim communities in Mindanao and the Sulu Archipelago developed their own societies, traditions, systems of leadership, and Islamic identity. They also resisted foreign domination during the Spanish and American periods.
Conflicts and disagreements between the government and various Moro groups continued for decades.

Events such as the Jabidah incident in 1968 contributed to the growth of the Moro struggle for self-determination. The Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF), and later the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), became important groups in the history of this struggle.
A significant step toward autonomy came in 1989 with the establishment of the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM) through Republic Act (RA) 6734.

The ARMM was later strengthened and expanded through RA 9054 in 2001. These laws provided an autonomous government for Muslim-majority areas of Mindanao within the framework of the Philippine Constitution.

On September 2, 1996, the government and the MNLF formally signed a peace agreement that ended a quarter of a century of fratricidal war in Mindanao. It was concluded after four years of tough negotiations held in Libya, Jakarta, Indonesia, and Mindanao.

At the same time, peace talks were ongoing from 1997 to 1999 with the MILF, a breakaway faction of the MNLF. In March 2000, then-president Joseph Estrada declared an all-out war against the group, which prompted it to withdraw from the negotiations.
The talks were formally resumed in 2001 under then-president Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo.
Here’s a timeline of the negotiations with the MILF that paved the way to the establishment of the autonomous region:
March 2001: The government and the MILF signed the Agreement on the General Framework for the Resumption of Peace Talks.

June 2001: The Tripoli Agreement on Peace was signed, with Libya and Malaysia playing important facilitating roles. The agreement centered on security, ancestral domain, and rehabilitation and development.
May 2002: The Joint Communiqué establishing the Ad Hoc Joint Action Group was signed as a form of cooperation against criminal groups in areas associated with the MILF.

2004: Malaysia became more involved with the creation of the International Monitoring Team, which helped oversee the ceasefire and contributed to confidence-building between the government and the MILF.

July 2008: The government and the MILF negotiated a Memorandum of Agreement on Ancestral Domain (MOA-AD) in July 2008. It was supposed to be signed on August 5, 2008, in Kuala Lumpur. However, the Supreme Court issued a temporary restraining order on August 4, 2008, preventing the signing. Violence subsequently erupted involving MILF breakaway elements, which displaced thousands.
July 2009: The government and the MILF agreed to mechanisms for suspending military operations.
June 2010: The government and MILF signed the Declaration of Continuity for the Peace Negotiations ahead of the takeover of the Aquino administration.
October 2012: The government and the MILF signed the Framework Agreement on the Bangsamoro, which set the foundation for creating a new autonomous political entity called the Bangsamoro.
March 2014: The government and the MILF signed the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro, described as the culmination of years of negotiations between the two sides.

July 2018: Republic Act 11054, or the Organic Law for the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (Bangsamoro Organic Law or BOL), was signed by then President Rodrigo Duterte. The law created the legal framework for the BARMM, replacing the ARMM. It aims to provide the Bangsamoro with a greater degree of self-government while still remaining part of the Philippines.
January 2019: The BOL was ratified through a plebiscite. A second plebiscite was held in February 2019. These enabled the establishment of the BARMM.

The BARMM currently consists of the provinces of Basilan (excluding Isabela City), Lanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Maguindanao del Sur, and Tawi-Tawi; the cities of Cotabato, Marawi, and Lamitan; and eight municipalities in North Cotabato that voted for inclusion in 2019.
Sulu, although originally included in BARMM after the 2019 plebiscite, was excluded following a 2024 Supreme Court ruling because the province voted against ratifying the Bangsamoro Organic Law.
Commemorating the seventh year of the BARMM's establishment in January 2026, Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua said the region is solid in moving toward a single direction.

“Seven years ago, BARMM was born not out of comfort but from conviction. It grows from a long and difficult history in which we endured conflict, displacement, and neglect. Yet, we never surrender our faith, our dignity, and our right to decide our own future,” said Macacua.

“BARMM today stands as a symbol of unity. We came from different paths and perspectives, yet we learned that no institution can stand, and no progress can last, if we work against one another,” he added. —LDF, GMA News

blocks.caption: BARMM Parliamentary Elections

blocks.text: Enacted in 2018, Republic Act No. 11054, or the Bangsamoro Organic Law, established the region's governmental structure and political entity to exercise self-governance according to the Philippine Constitution.
Under the law, BARMM was established with a “parliamentary form of government,” constituting a democratic political system that allows its people to freely vote (Sec. 3, Article IV).
But what does it mean to be parliamentary?
Parliamentary seats
The BARMM Parliament is composed of 80 members.
The seats are divided into three classifications and will be allocated as follows:
Regional Parliamentary Party Representatives (RPPP) seats are contested in a region-wide race among registered political parties, rather than individual candidates.
Each political party must submit a list of 40 nominees, ranked in order of priority to fill the seats won based on the overall votes gathered.
Think of it like the party-list representatives in the House of Representatives, who similarly rank their first, second, third, and subsequent nominees in case they win multiple seats.

According to the Botong Bangsamoro website, as far as practicable, at least one in every three party nominees must be a woman, and no nominee can be related to another within the second degree of consanguinity or affinity.
RPPP seats are allocated to political parties proportionally based on the percentage of votes obtained by each party relative to the total votes cast in the election.
Parties need at least 2.5% of the total valid votes to qualify, according to Comelec.
If qualifying groups receive varying percentages of votes, they will be ranked from highest to lowest, and the 40 seats will be distributed proportionally based on their vote shares.
For example, if a party secures 10% of the total RPPP votes across BARMM, it would earn roughly 4 seats (or 10 percent of the 40 available seats).
Meanwhile, Parliamentary District seats are awarded to representatives elected from single-member districts as follows:
Unlike RPPP seats, district representatives are elected through a direct plurality vote, meaning whoever gets the most votes wins.

Lastly, the remaining eight seats reserved for Sectoral representatives are divided among Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples (NMIP) and Settler Communities with two seats each, alongside one seat each for Women, Youth, Traditional Leaders, and the Ulama.
However, voters will not vote for the two NMIP representatives on the main election ballot; instead, their own assembly will select them under rules set by the Commission on Elections (Comelec).
Chief Minister
The position of “Chief Minister” is not directly voted on by the public. Instead, it is collectively chosen through a majority vote among the 80 elected members of the Parliament.
This parliamentary power marks a milestone, as the Chief Minister was previously appointed by the President of the Philippines.

According to the Bangsamoro Organic Law, the responsibilities of the Chief Minister include serving as the head of the Bangsamoro Government and exercising the power to appoint heads of ministries, agencies, bureaus, and other offices within the regional executive branch.
Decisions made by the Chief Minister and their appointed cabinet members directly impact constituents across social services, education, security, and livelihoods.
Once seated, the Chief Minister is also responsible for nominating candidates for two Deputy Chief Minister positions, who are then elected by the members of Parliament.
BARMM is divided into three subregions: Southwestern Mindanao, North-Central Mindanao, and South-Central Mindanao.
Under the law, the two Deputy Chief Ministers must represent the two subregions different from that of the elected Chief Minister.
Qualifications
In general, to qualify as a parliamentary nominee, a candidate must meet the following criteria:

items: At least 25 years old on election day
Youth representatives must be at least 18 years old and no older than 30 years old on election day

blocks.text: In addition, candidates for district representatives must specifically be registered voters of the district they seek to represent and must have resided there for at least one year immediately preceding election day.
Duties and term in office
According to the Bangsamoro website, elected members of the BARMM Parliament carry out vital legislative duties, including enacting laws, holding public consultations, and disciplining their members.
Under the law, members of Parliament are tasked with the following duties:

items: Enact laws that advance, protect, and ensure the general welfare of the people in the Bangsamoro region
Authorize the Chief Minister, Parliament Speaker, and Presiding Justice of the Shari'ah High Court to augment items in the general appropriations law (budget)
Regulate the grant of regional franchises and concessions, and empower the Chief Minister to grant leases, permits, and licenses over agricultural lands and forest management
Call for referendum on critical issues affecting BARMM
Conduct inquiries to assist in drafting legislation
Exercise disciplinary authority over members of Parliament
Consult on matters affecting the environment

blocks.text: The elected BARMM officials in the upcoming first-ever polls will serve an extended five-year term starting at noon on October 30, 2026 until noon on June 30, 2031.

The Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA) will continue to serve as the interim government until the newly elected leaders take office, unless members are replaced by the President or elected to a different position.
Following this initial transition, standard terms for Parliament members will revert to three years under Sec. 11, Article VII of the Bangsamoro Organic Law, with a limit of three consecutive terms.
To sync the BARMM polls with the national and local elections moving forward, the next regular Bangsamoro elections will be held on the second Monday of May 2031 and every three years after that.
Voting process
The first regular elections on September 14 will utilize an Automated Election System featuring Automated Counting Machines (ACMs).
This means voters will shade their choices on paper ballots and feed them into the ACMs, which will print a receipt reflecting their selected candidates.
On election day, voters must shade their choices as follows:

items: Six (6) Sectoral Representatives (2 for Settler Communities, and 1 each for Women, Youth, Ulama, and Traditional Leaders)

blocks.text: Voters are allowed to bring a list or cheat sheet (kodigo) of their chosen candidates, provided it reflects their personal preferences.
Political party logos will appear beside party names on the ballot for easy identification, though individual party nominees will not be listed.
For individual candidate races, photos will be printed alongside names to prevent voter confusion among candidates with similar names.
For accessibility, ballots will be available in Filipino, English, and Arabic.
Comelec previously stated that it aims to proclaim the winning BARMM candidates within two days after election day, citing the efficiency of automated counting. —Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/LDF, GMA News

blocks.caption: BARMM Elections 2026

blocks.text: The Philippine National Police (PNP) and the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) have deployed thousands of troops to ensure the safe and orderly conduct of the first parliamentary elections of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).
The PNP said it is stepping up its security measures in 108 election areas of concern (EAC) identified by the Commission on Elections (Comelec).
Of the total EACs, 15 areas were placed in the green category, 39 under yellow, 27 under orange, and another 27 under red.
What does it mean for an area to be classified as an EAC?
According to the Comelec, green areas have no security concerns or is relatively peaceful and orderly.

Yellow areas are those with suspected election-related incidents (ERIs) in the last two elections, politically motivated ERIs during the current election period, intense partisan rivalry, or a history of being placed under COMELEC control.
Orange locations have two or more factors under the yellow category, or exhibit serious armed threats.

Red category sites have one or more factors identified under the yellow and/or orange categories, along with serious armed threats or the existence of any ground for the declaration of COMELEC control.

In Comelec's most recent list heading into the polls, Lanao del Sur has the most red areas with 21, followed by Maguindanao with a distant 3. Basilan and Maguindanao del Norte have 1 each. Tugunan—a newly created town located in Cotabato province—was likewise listed under the red category.

Less than three weeks ahead of the polls, Comelec chairperson George Garcia said no areas in the BARMM are under the control of the poll body, following the recent ambush involving the region’s Interim Chief Minister, Abdulraof “Sammy Gambar” Macacua.

An area may be placed under Comelec control when there is intense political rivalry between or among candidates, political factions, or parties; or the presence of paramilitary forces, private armies, or terrorist groups.
On August 15, Macacua and his entourage escaped unharmed after armed assailants ambushed their convoy in Datu Odin Sinsuat.
Macacua was traveling from his hometown in Barangay Gambar, Mother Kabuntalan, when the incident occurred.

He attended the proclamation rally of the Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), the party he recently joined and where he was named chairman after previously running as an independent candidate in the province’s 3rd district.
—Mariel Celine Serquiña/VDV, GMA News
What to do before, during, after voting
After four postponements, it's all systems go for the parliamentary election in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).
To all BARMM voters, here is a practical guide to navigate election day safely and smoothly.
Before the vote
On September 13, the day before the election, a nationwide liquor ban will take effect, as indicated on the official Commission on Elections (Comelec) calendar.
Be sure to adhere to all election regulations, including restrictions related to illegal campaigning, carrying of weapons under the active gun ban, and vote-buying or selling.
When you cast your ballot, you are permitted to bring a prepared list or cheat sheet ("kodigo") of your selected candidates, provided it reflects your own personal choices.
You may prepare your selections for the following positions in advance:

items: Six (6) Sectoral Representatives (2 for Settler Communities, and 1 each for Women, Youth, Ulama, and Traditional Leaders)

blocks.text: To avoid delays, verify your polling precinct ahead of time using Comelec's online precinct finder:
Your designated polling location may be a public school, barangay hall, or other community facility.
To search for your precinct details, enter your full registered name, date of birth, and place of registration.
Voting day
On election day, priority voters can take advantage of designated early voting hours from 5 a.m. to 7 a.m. They include senior citizens, persons with disabilities (PWDs), and pregnant women.
Regular voting hours run from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
Priority voters could still vote during regular voting hours and would still be given priority access in line.
According to the Comelec, priority voters may proceed to the following designated areas:

items: Accessible Polling Places (APPs): Set up for PWDs, senior citizens, and pregnant voters who previously requested an APP setup on their voter registration records.
Priority Polling Places (PPPs): Designated areas within the voting center specifically arranged for PWDs, senior citizens, and pregnant voters who have difficulty walking or climbing stairs.

blocks.text: All designated priority polling areas are located exclusively on the ground floor of voting centers.
Shading of ballots

The election will utilize Automated Counting Machines (ACMs). This means voters will shade their selections on paper ballots and feed them into the ACMs, which will then print a paper audit trail (voter receipt) reflecting their chosen candidates.
Upon arriving at your assigned precinct and room, present yourself to the Electoral Board and state your full name and precinct number clearly.
Take note: a voter's ID is not required to vote. However, in case they need further verification of your identity, it is best to bring valid IDs.
The board will issue you: (1) a ballot; and (2) a secrecy folder. Inspect your ballot before sitting down to ensure it is clean, blank, and unmarked.
You may refer to your candidate list ("kodigo") while filling out your ballot.
To prevent confusion, political party names will be indicated on the ballot alongside their official logos.
Take note of the political party's name and not their nominees as the latter will not be printed on the ballot.
For individual candidate races, candidate photographs will be printed beside their names to help voters distinguish candidates with similar names.
For accessibility, ballots are printed in Filipino, English, and Arabic.
After completing your ballot, feed it directly into the ACM, which will process the paper and print your voting receipt.
Take your time to carefully review your receipt and confirm that it accurately records all your choices before placing it in the designated drop box.
Finally, to signify that you have exercised your right to vote, indelible ink will be applied to your forefinger before you exit the room.
Participating in the vote is a vital civic responsibility, but a voter's duty does not end once the ink dries.

As Comelec tallies the votes—targeting a full proclamation within two days—stay engaged, monitor official election updates closely, and help ensure an orderly outcome for the region. —Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Remilitarisation and support for Ukraine must not slacken, US tells Europe
articles.summary:
Comments in virtual meeting aimed at securing 300 Patriot missiles for Kyiv come as UK commits £100m for Ukraine’s air defences

The US undersecretary of defence, Elbridge Colby, told…

blocks.text: The US undersecretary of defence, Elbridge Colby, told European countries they “must not slacken” in their remilitarisation and their backing for Ukraine in a virtual meeting aimed at securing 300 Patriot interceptors for Kyiv.

The influential Pentagon official praised Ukraine’s recent “stout defence”, which he said proved that Europe was capable of leading the defence of its own continent from Russian aggression rather than relying on the US.

“Support for Ukraine contributes to Europe’s security,” Colby said at the start of a 50-country virtual meeting of the Ukraine contact group, reflecting what appears to be a warmer tone from the US on Ukraine.

It helped, he continued, “to rebuild Europe’s military strength and industrial capacity. But words are not enough. Real money and industrial capacity must be put to work. Again, I underline that this is happening, but we must not slacken.”

Led by its president, Donald Trump, the US has been pushing for Europe to dramatically increase defence spending and pay to supply American weapons, such as Patriot interceptors, to Kyiv, via a scheme set up by Nato.

The UK announced it had committed £100m to boost Ukraine’s air defences over winter by buying a package of US military equipment that will include urgently needed Patriot missiles, before the meeting had started.

Boris Pistorius, the German defence minister, pledged in his opening remarks that Berlin would donate a number of older Patriot Pac-2 interceptors from army stocks, and urged other allies of Ukraine to follow suit.

Ukraine is currently unable to prevent Russian ballistic missile attacks because of a shortage of Patriot interceptors, leading to attacks that have killed civilians and destroyed food and logistics warehouses over the summer.

Wes Streeting, the UK defence secretary, said that Ukraine had been “pretty clear” about what it needed: “Three hundred Patriot missiles from partner stocks, 500 air-to-air interceptors with counter-cruise missile capability, $2bn for drones,” and continued contributions to other schemes.
The UK did not say how many Patriots it would be able to buy, but the number is likely to be only a fraction of the number sought, given the cost of each interceptor is estimated at about $3m.

Yehven Khamarra, Ukraine’s newly appointed defence minister, acknowledged that Ukraine’s “situation with ballistics is much more difficult” and which was “precisely down to a lack of Patriot missiles”. It was a situation, he added, that the Kremlin was aware of, and trying to exploit.
after newsletter promotion

The Ukrainian minister also said that Ukraine faced a defence budget gap of €23bn this year, and he hoped that countries would bring forward more funding so that its drone investment programme could continue uninterrupted. Kyiv hopes that the EU will bring forward some of a €90bn two-year loan to help plug the shortfall.

An escalation of the long-range war has meant that the harm to civilians is increasing as Ukraine targets Russian oil refineries and warehouses, while Russian bombing has meant that civilian casualties in Ukraine are at their highest level since May 2022 amid near constant attacks on the country’s cities.

On Sunday, US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited Kyiv for the first time, to discuss peace proposals, though no breakthrough was made. A day earlier they had visited the Kremlin, which is still pressing for Ukraine to give up territory and make a string of concessions for ending the war.
The prime minister, Andy Burnham, spoke to tTrump about the war on Monday, with the two agreeing on the need to “continue working towards a ceasefire that prevented more loss of life”.

articles.title: Israel to close British consulate in Jerusalem after sanctions announced
articles.summary: Several MPs also banned from Israel after UK steps up condemnation of settlements and announces sweeping sanctions

blocks.text: Israel has ordered the closure of the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem in response to sweeping UK sanctions on goods from illegal settlements.

Reacting to Ed Miliband’s description of violent Jewish settler activity on the occupied Palestinian West Bank as “ethnic cleansing” carried out with the tacit backing of the Netanyahu government, Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, announced retaliatory measures including the closure of the consulate and entry bans on several UK MPs.
It is the latest stage in a furious and escalating row between the countries in which diplomatic relations have hit rock bottom.

The consulate in the Sheikh Jarrah area of the city focuses on Palestinian issues in the occupied territories, including Gaza, the West Bank and Jerusalem. The British embassy in Tel Aviv is where the UK’s ambassador to Israel is based.
While most countries regard East Jerusalem as illegally occupied by Israel since the Six Day War in 1967, Israel says Jerusalem is its undivided capital.

“United Jerusalem is the capital of Israel and is under its full sovereignty,” Sa’ar said. “Any foreign activity in the area must be conducted through accepted and agreed channels and without violating Israel’s sovereignty.”

Sa’ar also announced entry bans on a number of mostly leftwing MPs including the former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, the Your Party MP Zarah Sultana, the Labour MPs Diane Abbott, Naz Shah, John McDonnell and Richard Burgon and the Green MPs Hannah Spencer, Carla Denyer, Siân Berry and Ellie Chowns.

The Israeli government added that longstanding British involvement in the training of Palestinian security forces on the West Bank would be terminated. Britain will also be excluded from the US-led Gaza coordination mission, which is based in Israel.
The British sanctions were coordinated with 11 other countries, including France and Canada.
Sa’ar said: “The British move is morally distorted, ​and constitutes blatant interference in the affairs of a sovereign state and its electoral process.”

He added: “Israel has nothing against the British people. We know that we have many friends in Britain. Unfortunately, a hostile Labour government is in office, systematically acting against the state of Israel, and it has left us with no choice but to finally respond to its hostile actions.”

blocks.caption: Gideon Sa’ar, Israel’s foreign minister, described the UK’s actions as ‘morally distorted’.  Photograph: Abir Sultan/EPA

blocks.text: Sa’ar said that he ​had coordinated ‌Israel’s response ​with the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. Israel will hold an election in late October.
Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, called the ban “a grave miscalculation, a decision that will fall on the wrong side of history”.

“In the current context, it would be a gross interference in the democratic elections of a sovereign nation,” he said. “Sanctions are not a solution – dialogue is. I say to all foreign governments: Stop. Step away from the dead-end of sanctions and boycotts, and turn toward constructive dialogue and toward cooperation.”

Settlement building and settlement-related violence have increased under the auspices of far-right Israeli ministers in the Netanyahu government who have said publicly that they aim to “bury” a two state solution through their actions.

Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel’s hardline public security minister and a settler leader, called on Netanyahu to recognise Argentina’s claim to the Falkland Islands, a British overseas territory in the South Atlantic known in Argentina as Islas Malvinas.

blocks.caption: Palestinians attend the funeral on Monday of a young man who died after being shot in the head when Israeli settlers raided a village.  Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, a longtime supporter of the settlements, said the British sanctions were “discrimination against the Jewish people”. He said the UK could face “repercussions or retaliations” from the US.

However, in a markedly more muted response, US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said Washington would ‌not follow Britain, ​France and Canada in blocking ⁠imports from Israeli ​settlements in ​the Palestinian ​territory and did not want to see moves that would destabilise the West Bank.

Israel has been under notice from successive British governments – both Conservative and Labour – for years over the risk of international isolation and potential sanctions related to continuing settlement activity in the occupied territories. These warnings have becomelouder in recent years as violent settler activity has escalated.
The UK’s Labour government previously sanctioned some Israeli settlers and illegal outposts over violence against Palestinians and illegal development in the West Bank.
In a change of Britain’s position, Miliband, the foreign secretary, said on Tuesday that the UK regards Israel’s occupation of the West Bank, and not just the settlements, as illegal.
The tougher stance is likely to be welcomed by many Labour voters and lawmakers, who have urged the government to go further in sanctioning Israel and supporting Palestinians.

Difficulties to establishing an EU-wide approach, coordinated with the UK, had led to countries making individual decisions on a widening sanctions regime that culminated in the joint statement by 12 countries that they were setting in train the process of far harder-hitting sanctions.

articles.title: EU, UK express dismay over Mladic funeral in Serbia
articles.summary: The EU is deliberating an official response to the glorification of war criminal Ratko Mladic in Belgrade. The UK, meanwhile, summoned Serbia's charge d'affaires over the display.

image.caption: Mladic commanded the Army of Republika Srpska during the 1992-1995 war in BosniaImage: Oliver Bunic/AFP

blocks.text: Both the EU and UK on Tuesday expressed dismay over the funeral in Belgrade, Serbia of late war criminal Ratko Mladic a day prior.

Thousands of people, including at least six Serbian ministers, attended the event on Monday which was seen as glorifying Mladic. He received military honors at the funeral, with the head of Serbia's Orthodox Church presiding over the ceremony.

The Bosnian Serb commander died last month at The Hague, where he had been imprisoned for life. Mladic was convicted in 2017 of genocide, having orchestrated the July 1995 Srebrenica massacre, where 8,000 Bosniak men and boys were killed.
Mladic, called the "Butcher of Bosnia" by some international press, is a revered as a war hero by many Serbian nationalists in both Serbia and Bosnia.
EU leader call Mladic state funeral 'deeply regrettable'
EU leaders condemned the funeral, with the bloc weighing an official response to the event.

"The elements of official support and the presence of some senior Serbian officials at the funeral are deeply regrettable," European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa said in statements posted on X.
"They demonstrate a failure to confront a dark chapter in Europe's recent history and contradict the values underpinning Serbia's path towards the European Union," they added.
A European Commission spokeperson, in comments to German news agency DPA, said next steps were being evaluated.

EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas added: "Serbia's path into the European Union requires an unequivocal commitment in fundamental European values and historical truth."
Serbia first applied for EU membership in 2009. Serbia's EU candidacy was confirmed by the European Council in 2012.
Serbia: Thousands attend 'Butcher of Bosnia' funeral
UK summons Serbian envoy
The UK, meanwhile, summoned Serbia's charge d'affaires in response to the funeral.
"As a military commander, Mladic presided over crimes that are among the worst committed in Europe since the Second World War," the British Foreign Office said in a statement.
"The thoughts of the UK Government are with Mladic's victims and their families. They deserve respect, compassion and accountability, not efforts to rewrite proven history," the statement added.

The UK said that the "glorification of a convicted war criminal directly undermines trust, fuels division, and is incompatible with the process of reconciliation within Bosnia and Herzegovina and the region."
Bosnia expels Serbian diplomats, says Belgrade crossed 'red line'
In its reaction to the funeral, neighboring Bosnia expelled two Serbian diplomats, saying Serbia crossed a "red line" in its display of reverence for Mladic.
"They crossed every red line with what they did yesterday, the day before, and in the days leading up to the reception," Bosnian Foreign Minister Elmedin Konakovic told a Sarajevo press event.
Konakovic had also said he would withdraw most staff from the Bosnian Embassy in Belgrade in an effort to reduce ties to "the lowest possible level"

Serbian President Aleksander Vucic was not present at Mladic's funeral, although his son Danilo, did attend the event. Vucic rejected allegations that Mladic was being glorified at the funeral and said the event was put together by Mladic's family rather than the state.
However, the presence of soldiers and government ministers at the funeral, as well as the use of a government plane to bring Mladic's body to Belgrade, have sparked outrage.
Can Serbia's student movement turn protest into power?

The controversial funeral comes ahead of snap elections next month. Serbia has faced a political crisis in the past two years triggered by the collapse of a concrete canopy at a railway station in Novi Sad.

articles.title: Prince George starts Eton College as Harry and Meghan grapple with 'brutal put-down'
articles.summary: It was a day of ups and downs for the Royal Family as, on the one hand, Prince George started his first day at prestigious Eton College but, on the other, Prince Harry and Meghan grappled with their…

image.caption: Catherine, Princess of Wales, left, and Prince William, right, walk with their 13-year-old son, Prince George, as he arrives for his first day at Eton College, in Eton, west of London, England, on Tuesday. (Adrian Dennis/AFP/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

It was a day of ups and downs for the Royal Family as, on the one hand, Prince George started his first day at prestigious Eton College but, on the other, Prince Harry and Meghan grappled with their status as non-working members of the Royal Family.
Harry, Meghan surprised by King's confirmation they will remain non-working members of Royal Family

It was a day of ups and downs for the Royal Family as, on the one hand, Prince George started his first day at prestigious Eton College and, on the other, Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, grappled with their status as non-working members of the Royal Family.

The Prince and Princess of Wales were all smiles as Prince George started his first day at the 600-year-old school Tuesday morning, following in his father's footsteps. The trio appeared relaxed as they dropped off George, King Charles's 13-year-old grandson and second in line to the throne.
"Welcome, good luck and enjoy," said headteacher Simon Henderson, shaking hands with George before ushering everyone inside to the school where George will be boarding.
Later, George was photographed grinning in his new school uniform: a black tailcoat, waistcoat and a white collar.

Eton is the alma mater for many of ​the ⁠country's elite, including Prince William and Prince Harry, and has educated 20 British prime ministers, including Boris Johnson and David Cameron, as well as actors Hugh Laurie, Damian ⁠Lewis ​and Tom Hiddleston.

As BBC reports, George's time at Eton will likely see him somewhat shielded from media and public attention. Prince William has previously spoken about much he enjoyed being "just another student" at the school.
Harry and Meghan 'surprised' by letter
On the other hand, Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan, experienced what some observers are calling a rude awakening back in the U.K. after Charles confirmed Monday they will remain non-working royals.

The news, which came in the form of a letter from Buckingham Palace sent to senior British officials, said that after ​Harry and Meghan stepped down from official royal duties in 2020, they "are no longer working members ​of the Royal Family."
"In short, their position is akin to ​private citizens with commercial and charitable interests," the letter stated.

items: The 'shockwaves' of Prince Harry and Meghan's return to the U.K.
Charles confirms Harry and Meghan to remain non-working royals after their return to U.K.

blocks.text: On Tuesday, The Associated Press reported that the Duke and Duchess of Sussex were surprised by the way Buckingham Palace released the letter. It caught the couple off guard when it was released to the media on Monday in part because they were given little time to review or comment on its contents, a person familiar with the discussions told AP.
They were "a little surprised not to have been told about this in advance," their representative said in a statement on Tuesday, as reported by BBC.

The couple’s representatives received a copy of the letter just one hour and 12 minutes before it was released to news outlets, the person said. That left them with little time to respond because they were unable to reach Harry, who was in a meeting, until just two minutes before the letter was released, the person added.
The letter reiterates the palace's previous stance.

Harry and Meghan stepped back from royal duties in 2020 when they moved to North America to make their own living, turning to ventures such as deals with Netflix and Spotify. At the time, Queen Elizabeth made clear that the couple could not be part-time royals. Charles reiterated that position after he became King in 2022.
Harry and Meghan moving back to the U.K.
'Warning shot'
In an interview with GB News, royal historian Alexander Larman called Charles' move a "brutal put-down."
"I would call it a right royal knees-up, actually, because Harry's just been back a couple of weeks now and we're seeing how it's all going for him," Larman said.

"This is basically the King saying: 'You're back, I'm delighted on a paternal level that you're back. But, as head of a firm, I'm making it very, very clear that you are not back in the Royal Family."

As CBC's The Royal Fascinator reported over the weekend, Harry and Meghan's return to the U.K. set off shockwaves because it seems so counterintuitive and contradictory to everything that they have said since they left.
Royal expert Phil Dampier told The Sun the King's statement was a "warning shot" not to overshadow the Royal Family.
"It’s really sending out a message — a warning shot across their bows, you could say. What they’re [the palace] emphasizing is that nothing has changed as far as they’re concerned," Dampier said.

"Now that they’ve come back and might start turning up to various charity events or doing commercial activities, it’s got to be absolutely clear to everyone that they are doing it as private individuals and not as royals.”
On Monday, Meghan posted a photo on her As Ever Instagram account, in which she relaxes on a lawn with the couple's black lab, Pula. "Long weekend plans," notes the caption.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Natalie Stechyson has been a writer and editor at CBC News since 2021. She covers stories on social trends, families, gender, human interest, as well as general news. She's worked as a journalist since 2009, with stints at the Globe and Mail and Postmedia News, among others. Before joining CBC News, she was the parents editor at HuffPost Canada, where she won a silver Canadian Online Publishing Award for her work on pregnancy loss. You can reach her at natalie.stechyson@cbc.ca.
With files from Reuters, the Associated Press and CBC's The Royal Fascinator

articles.title: British widow faces deportation from Sweden after 22 years
articles.summary: A 78-year-old British woman is facing deportation for failing to fill out a Brexit residence application on time.

blocks.text: A 78-year-old British widow has told the BBC she is struggling to eat or sleep as the Swedish government threatens to deport her over a late post-Brexit residence application.
Joyce Thomas, a retired nurse, moved to Sweden 22 years ago with her husband, who passed away from cancer three years ago.
This came after they were informed by the Swedish authorities that they should have made a formal application to stay in the country after Brexit.
Thomas has since had numerous applications and appeals rejected, and Tuesday marks the latest deadline for her to leave voluntarily.
"This is absolute hell," she said from her home in Sweden.
"I can't sleep, I can't eat. You get up in the morning, you don't know what's going to happen."

The Swedish migration minister told the BBC that the government will "examine whether there are measures we can take to make the process easier for those affected" by some consequences of the EU-UK withdrawal agreement.
When the UK left the EU on 31 January 2020, British citizens stopped being EU citizens, which meant they could no longer stay in Sweden with right of residence status.
During a transitional period, British citizens could apply for residence status under the withdrawal agreement between the UK and the EU - which ended on 31 December 2021.
Thomas said she and her husband were unaware that they needed to submit an application and she was only informed of the rule once she attempted to re-enter the country in 2023.
After years of appeals, the Migrationsverket, the Swedish government agency responsible for migration, told her last month that her voluntary departure deadline was 8 September.
Her lawyers are arguing against the deportation, but she is still waiting to hear from the government.
Thomas said the possibility of having to leave her son, grandchildren, friends and husband's grave has become too much to bear.
"I'm tired, I really am tired and I'm not young anymore," she said.
"Where is the empathy? I've lived here for more than 20 years - I've got friends, I've got family."

According to Eurostat data, between 2021 and 2025, 2,490 UK nationals were ordered to leave Sweden. This is almost a third of more than 7,500 UK nationals ordered to leave the 27 EU Member States over this time period.
The Migrationsverket said it could not comment on Thomas's case without her consent and did not respond to a question about how many British nationals are at risk of deportation.
However, it told the Guardian last week that 458 British citizens had been deported or forcibly removed since Brexit.

Last month, a family told the BBC how their father, who has dementia and vascular parkinsonism and is living in full-time care in Sweden, was also threatened with removal after more than two decades in the country.

Swedish minister for migration, Johan Forssell, told the BBC that the current framework was implemented by a previous government and that it "will therefore look closely at the situation and examine whether there are measures we can take to make the process easier for those affected".
He did not address Thomas's case directly but said "the government believes the rules should be applied generously".
"The UK is a very important partner for Sweden, and we want British citizens who live and work in Sweden to be able to remain here," he said.
"We are currently in dialogue with the relevant Swedish authorities to get a clearer picture of what measures may be possible," he added.

A spokesperson from the the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office said: "We welcome the statement from the Swedish authorities that they will look at this issue. We are ready to support them in doing so."

articles.title: 'That’s not storytelling': Olympians hope proposed guidelines eliminate sexualization on broadcasts
articles.summary: A report from The Representation Project from the Tokyo 2021 Olympics found that women were sexualized nearly 10 times more than male athletes at the Games, despite Olympic broadcasters encouraging…

image.caption: Canada's Kate Van Buskirk refers to her track uniform as her 'equipment.' (Arnd Wiegmann/Reuters)

blocks.text: A report from The Representation Project from the Tokyo 2021 Olympics found that women were sexualized nearly 10 times more than male athletes at the Games, despite Olympic broadcasters encouraging "sport appeal, not sex appeal" to camera operators ahead of the competition.
'It should be about performance, not appearance,' says Canadian Olympian Kate Van Buskirk
When Kate Van Buskirk made her Olympic debut at Tokyo 2021, she clocked her second fastest time in the women’s 5,000 metres in a sweltering 41 C.
It was a massive feat, and afterward, she collapsed onto the track to soak it all in.

Five years later, Van Buskirk recalls the moment to be the most “egregious” time she was captured on camera, with photos posted online of her “sprawled out” on the track from extremely invasive angels.

“I've just finished the biggest race of my life … I just remember looking at those and thinking, ‘these live on the Internet forever,’” Van Buskirk said, adding that there were other photos of the moment that didn’t show her inappropriately.
Instances like this aren’t rare in women’s sports.

“It should be about performance, not appearance,” said Van Buskirk, who has since retired and works as a track and field analyst. “Even if it's passive and unintentional, there should be thought put around how we position photographers so that we're not giving them just that one angle.”

For decades, women’s sports uniforms have been a point of conversation regarding coverage and fit, such as the controversy ahead of Paris 2024 when Nike unveiled its new Team USA track and field kit for women as a high-cut bodysuit.
Van Buskirk refers to her track uniform as her “equipment,” opting for bottoms called “bunners.”

“I want to wear as little fabric as possible while still feeling like I have the dignity to do what I'm doing and be taken seriously as an athlete, but also not have to be distracted by that and worry about am I literally covering my private areas,” she added.
When does a sports replay go from storytelling to sexualization?
Europe pushing for change from broadcasters

In July 2026 the European Broadcasting Union and European Athletics created new guidelines to improve coverage in women’s athletics, calling out problematic broadcasting habits that “add zero narrative value.”
Lingering close-ups on specific body parts, low-angle camera placements, and excessive slow-motion replays with no storytelling purpose are the main “culprits” the report, Raising The Bar, cited.
“The way people consume sport today can amplify that impact. A single frame from a live
broadcast can be clipped, zoomed in and shared around the world within minutes,” Elissavet Arapi, women's sport lead for the European Broadcasting Union, said.
“Those images can then attract sexualized comments and abusive behaviour online, and athletes have told us they are increasingly concerned about that.”
Van Buskirk shared that some of her peers in athletics have found highly sexualized photos taken of them in competition on “soft core porn” sites.

“I have seen, again, many replays over the years of myself and others where there's no commentary over top of it … It’s a slow motion pan up, usually starting around the calves and coming up really slowly,” she said.

Arapi says that navigating editorial decisions like this is a collaborative effort amongst directors, video operators, and camera operators who need to “react quickly if their shot gives us a sexualized image.”
Michele Donnelly, associate professor of Sports Management at Brock University, is quick to call out the limitations of the guidelines.

“Why can't it be a policy? The entire document makes the case for why this is necessary. It should rise to the level of something that is a requirement, not simply a guideline,” Donnelly said. “The IOC (International Olympic Committee) needs to be the first one to demonstrate this is how you do it and to hold themselves accountable.”
As Canada’s official broadcaster of the Olympic Games, Paul McDougall, CBC Sports’ head of production and content, said the organization’s priority is always athletic excellence above all else.

"Broadcasters don’t just owe women athletes a spot on the screen; they owe them a broadcast that honours their power, skill and dignity. Visibility inspires participation. By adopting respectful production guidelines, we move beyond representation and commit to a landscape where athletic excellence is always the primary lens." McDougall said.
The Olympic Broadcasting Services (OBS), the permanent host of all Olympic and Paralympic Games, said they also have guidelines in place to ensure respectful coverage of athletes.

“Respectful and appropriate portrayal of all athletes in all sports is an integral part of OBS’ Olympic Games coverage. This is reflected in the OBS guidelines for venue production teams and is also taken into account through our production quality control processes when supervising OBS coverage,” the OBS shared in a statement to CBC Sports.
Education versus information
Back in 2019, the World Athletics Organization introduced two miniature cameras inside the starting blocks for sprint and hurdle events at the world championships in Doha.

While the goal was to provide “trailblazing” angles capturing the runner's explosion off the starting blocks, several sprinters heavily criticized the camera placement. Most notably German athletes Gina Lückenkemper and Tatjana Pinto, who said the upward facing cameras were intrusive and uncomfortable while wearing their competition attire.

“When your body is exposed…there's a presumption of access and ownership and being able to use images of women's bodies for whatever purposes people want to use them for. But also, that translates to in real life interactions with athletes and expectations of them,” Donnelly said.

In response to the push back, the International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF) agreed to only show shots from the block cameras right at the starting pistol and to delete video data at other times each day.

“We have noted some specific feedback about the block cameras and we have confirmed we have appropriate measures in place to protect athlete privacy during the process of selecting images for broadcast,” the IAAF wrote in a statement. “We also have strict editorial guidelines for what is broadcast and these have been observed since the beginning of the championships.”
While sexualization isn’t limited to women athletes, men in sport often celebrate when their bodies are captured on camera, rather than being at risk of threat, says Donnelly.

“Without diminishing the negative effects that there may be for many athletes, often when men's bodies are being sexualized in a celebratory way. Like, think of the poor high jumper [Anthony Ammirati] right, from Paris 2024 where it was all about his manhood and his masculinity.”
On Friday, the world's top track stars will compete at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest where heated rivalries and new stars will emerge in the leadup to LA 2028.
With all eyes on athletics as one of the most watched sports at the Summer Olympics, establishing broadcasting expectations may be more important than ever.

“There's a difference between informing and educating, versus entertaining. And I think as soon as we slip into entertainment, as the thing that we're focusing on, that's when it can really quickly devolve into hyper sexualization,” Van Buskirk said.
“That's not storytelling, that's objectification,” Van Buskirk said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Tara is a Toronto-based journalist who writes and produces athlete features for CBC Sports, exploring the intersection of sport, society, and culture. Prior to this, she was a writer for the CTV News national editorial team, covering trending and breaking news. Tara's bylines have appeared in Toronto Life, Canadian Business, and Maclean’s where she covers stories related to culture, entertainment, and sports. She holds a Master’s degree from Toronto Metropolitan University.

articles.title: Pinoy students improved in PISA 2025
articles.summary: Filipino students’ scores in reading, mathematics and science have improved significantly in the 2025 Program for International Student Assessment , Education Secretary Sonny Angara said…

blocks.text: September 9, 2026 | 12:00am
Education Secretary Sonny Angara. Department of Education
Department of Education

MANILA, Philippines — Filipino students’ scores in reading, mathematics and science have improved significantly in the 2025 Program for International Student Assessment (PISA), Education Secretary Sonny Angara said yesterday.
The Philippines recorded a mean score of 373 in science, 371 in mathematics and 367 in reading – up by 17, 16 and 20 points, respectively, from the country’s 2022 results.
Based on its mean score, the Philippines outranked 14 countries in science, 16 in math and 18 in reading.
More Filipinos reached level two or higher – the baseline proficiency level measured by PISA, Angara noted.

“This is a significant achievement for learners and the entire Philippine education system. But more than the numbers, we are seeing evidence that learners are capable of making real and meaningful progress,” he said.
The Philippine is the fastest improving country in terms of reading performance, Angara said, citing the 10-year trend analysis of the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development.
The OECD has grouped the Philippines among countries with notable improvement in mathematics.
In science, the country recorded a positive long-term trend despite an overall decline in science performance globally, the OECD noted.

articles.title: Bigger NOAH funding to boost disaster, climate change response
articles.summary: he recently released P1 billion will further expand Project Nationwide Operational Assessment of Hazards, focusing on strengthening flood management, hazard monitoring and disaster risk reduction…

blocks.text: September 9, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The recently released P1 billion will further expand Project Nationwide Operational Assessment of Hazards (NOAH), focusing on strengthening flood management, hazard monitoring and disaster risk reduction systems as the country confronts the effects of climate change.

In various interviews with PCO-Integrated State Media and private media outlets, UP Resilience Institute (UPRI) executive director Mahar Lagmay, a UP geology professor, said he hopes the government’s funding for UPRI “will continue to transform scientific knowledge into practical action that protects lives and helps build safer, more resilient and sustainable communities.”

President Marcos’ order to infuse P1 billion into Project NOAH, which UPRI manages, will boost impact-based forecasting developed by Project NOAH researchers using years of historical information, satellite images, rainfall data and other datasets.

This directive from President Marcos to the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) is another critical move in his data-driven governance, which recognizes the vital role of hard science in statecraft, notably the national infrastructure spending of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) being guided by scientific data from UPRI’s NOAH.

Founded in 2012, NOAH seeks to assist the country in disaster risk reduction and management, climate change adaptation and mitigation efforts and related activities through research, development and extension services.
Science-backed

For its part, the DPWH has begun laying the technical foundation for future, science-backed flood management infrastructure to strengthen long-term disaster preparedness and climate change risk response nationwide.

At President Marcos’ directive to enhance nationwide flood resiliency, Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon has ordered the updating of all flood management master plans to protect Filipinos from massive flooding year after year.

To ensure these master plans reflect current climate realities, the agency is collaborating with Project NOAH, local government units and key partner agencies to integrate detailed hazard mapping and scientific data before their implementation.
On Sept. 2, the President said the government is now implementing a flood control master plan that has been in place for decades.
“We already have a master plan. It’s just never been executed. We are only executing it now,” President Marcos told reporters after inspecting repair works at a collapsed bridge in Tarlac.
“We have had a master plan for decades pero walang ginawa. Ngayon lang natin sinisimulan (but nothing was done. We are only starting it now),” the President said.
The presidential remarks come as Central Luzon, Metro Manila and other parts of Luzon grapple with widespread flooding brought by heavy monsoon rains.

The administration has repeatedly called on national government agencies to implement long-term flood control measures, including de-clogging and dredging waterways, improving drainage systems and proper land-use planning, as the government responds to increasingly intense rainfall linked to climate change.
Faster, more accurate
Lagmay said NOAH’s impact-based forecasting system is projected to forecast, one day in advance, where flooding may occur and its impact on roads, homes, buildings and vehicular flow.

“The P1-billion allocation for UPRI will be measured by better information, transparency, evidence-based governance and decision-making, effective flood management and reduced disaster risks and losses,” Lagmay said.

Of the total allocation, P935 million will support research services, while P65 million will fund general management and supervision of NOAH’s implementation. The allocation is part of the UP System’s built-in appropriation under the 2026 General Appropriations Act.

Lagmay said UPRI’s budget will fund high-resolution mapping of major river basins, hazard assessments, land-use planning and Oplan Kontra Baha initiatives, in coordination with the DPWH, Metropolitan Manila Development Authority, local government units and private-sector partners.

The allocation will also support Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) drone topographic surveys, capacity-building programs with state universities and colleges, native tree mapping, sediment erosion assessments, mapping of hidden waterways, nature-based solutions and the use of artificial intelligence and analytics for disaster risk management.
UP president Angelo Jimenez said the Marcos administration’s funding for UPRI is “an investment in the power of research and innovation to serve the nation.”
“We do research because knowledge matters, and knowledge matters most when it can help us make better decisions, solve real problems and improve the lives of our people,” Jimenez said.

articles.title: Recantations can aid Martin, say House allies
articles.summary: Recantations of several witnesses in the flood control controversy could help weaken the plunder case against Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez, two of his allies said yesterday.

blocks.text: September 9, 2026 | 12:00am

Contributed photo shows a team led by PNP chief Jose Melencio Nartatez serving the arrest warrant on former speaker Martin Romualdez, who has a detainee’s shirt draped over his hospital clothing, at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center last night. Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla also went to the hospital.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — Recantations of several witnesses in the flood control controversy could help weaken the plunder case against Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez, two of his allies said yesterday.
Former congressman Robert Ace Barbers and Rep. Joel Chua said witnesses’ retraction of their testimonies implicating the former House speaker could serve as a mitigating factor in his case.
“Four or five of (18 men) have made their recantations. And this, I think, will have an impact when it reaches trial,” Barbers said. “What that impact will be, I still have no idea.”
“We respect the ombudsman’s findings and we expect that the former speaker will exhaust all the remedies to protect his right,” Chua said.
President Marcos did not intervene in the arrest of his cousin Romualdez, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said yesterday.

“Martin and I are also close, but in the interest of the State, we will do everything,” Remulla said, noting that he and his brother Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla belong to the same fraternity as Romualdez. – Emmanuel Tupas

articles.title: Suspect held in Germany after spate of sabotage attacks on power grid
articles.summary: The suspect had reportedly claimed responsibility for attacks on electricity substations in letters.

blocks.text: A 48-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of carrying out a spate of sabotage attacks on Germany's electricity grid after spending several days on the run.
The suspect was carrying explosives when he was detained near the Weisweiler power plant in western Germany on Tuesday, police in Cologne said.
A tent in nearby undergrowth was also found to be rigged with further explosives, they added.

The suspect, named by German media as Daniel V, is believed to have written letters claiming responsibility for the attacks, which have taken place in Brandenburg and Saxony in the east as well North Rhine-Westphalia in the west.
Police said explosives found during the arrest were being examined by a bomb disposal expert, while officers were checking to see if any undiscovered devices had been set up in the surrounding area.
Prior to the suspect's arrest on Tuesday, police said they had found several launch devices on high-voltage lines near the Weisweiler plant on Monday afternoon, alongside "another confession letter".
A series of incidents across the grid in the last week have followed a similar pattern, with rockets used to shoot wires across high-voltage cables in order to cause short circuits.
The attacks have led to power-generating units at some plants being temporarily taken off the grid.

A statement from the Cologne Public Prosecutor's Office and Cologne Police on Tuesday did not provide further details on the suspect, or on the number and whereabouts of incidents he has been linked to.

German media have previously reported receiving two letters from the suspect claiming responsibility for the attacks. The Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung said the handwritten letters contained information that had not yet been made public.

The letters were apparently signed with the first name Daniel, while his surname was kept anonymous, in line with German privacy rules. The letters also gave a residential address in the town of Gevelsberg.

Cologne Police had previously said it was searching for a 48-year-old suspect from the town in connection with the sabotage of electrical substations in three German states. Investigators had also said explosives were found during a search of the suspect's apartment.
In Saxony alone, police found 21 devices near high-voltage power lines last Friday and Saturday.
Interior Minister Armin Schuster has admitted it could have led to a regional blackout, but he has warned against jumping to conclusions.
"The way this deed was committed makes this case unusual, as well as the manner of the confession," he said.
